[gita-a00-v01] He who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience — whose one, given to contemplation, is thus the bond of nondifference: He, Śaṃbhura, woe-averting, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.

[gita-a00-v02] By the sage Dvaipāyana was this scripture expounded, measured by hundreds of thousands; here liberation is established as the fruit — and mādhānyataḥ [L0-fork], its other dharma-and-rest is recited to nourish it.

[gita-a00-v03] Liberation, by name, complete-differentiation in form, all-knowing, auspicious-natured in all instruments and more — free from need, in Bhagavān the Lord, ever-risen: dissolution — this much, toward it [prathiḥ L0-fork], in summary.

[gita-a00-v04] Although liberation by name is celebrated in other connections, yet the Bhagavadgītā is the giver of true attainment.

[gita-a00-v05] In them, although earlier ones made many expositions, yet my attempt too is reasonable — revealing its hidden meaning.

[gita-a00-v06] From the oral tradition of Bhaṭṭa Indurāja, examined long with thought, made by Abhinavagupta — this here is the Gītārthasaṃgraha.

[gita-a01-v01] The first adhyaya opens by defining who is fit to be taught, then presents Dhritarashtra's question about the gathered warriors.

[gita-a01-v02] Sanjaya says that seeing the Pandava army arrayed, King Duryodhana approached the teacher and spoke.

[gita-a01-v03] Duryodhana asks the teacher to look at the great arrayed army of Pandu's sons, arranged by Drupada's wise son, his disciple.

[gita-a01-v04] Here are heroes and great bowmen equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great chariot-fighter.

[gita-a01-v05] Dhrishtaketu and Cekitana, the valiant king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, best of men.

[gita-a01-v06] Yudhamanyu and valiant Uttamaujas, Saubhadra, and the Draupadeyas—all indeed great chariot-fighters.

[gita-a01-v07] But know, best of the twice-born, the distinguished leaders among us, for naming my army's commanders to you.

[gita-a01-v08] In the great army, all these hero-approved leaders are: you, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Shalya, Jayadratha, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and valiant Saumadatti.

[gita-a01-v09] And many other heroes, for my sake having abandoned life, armed with various weapons and skilled in various battles, are there.

[gita-a01-v10] What use is this enumeration? Our force, protected by Bhima, is insufficient; but their force, protected by Bhishma, is sufficient. The Pandava force protected by Bhimasena is ours and insufficient to conquer; or the force protected by Bhishma is related to these Pandavas and sufficient to conquer, if much is not conquerable by them in battle.

[gita-a01-v11] Stationed in all passages according to your portions, you all indeed must protect Bhishma.

[gita-a01-v12] Causing joy in him, the valiant Kuru elder and grandsire roared loudly and blew the conch.

[gita-a01-v13] Then conches, drums, paṇavas, anakas, and gomukhas were struck all at once, and that sound became tumultuous.

[gita-a01-v14] Then Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava, standing in the great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.

[gita-a01-v15] Hṛṣīkeśa blew Pāñcajanya, Dhanañjaya blew Devadatta, and Vṛkodara of terrible deeds blew Pauṇḍra, the great conch.

[gita-a01-v16] King Yudhiṣṭhira, Kuntī's son, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.

[gita-a01-v17] Kāśya, the supreme archer, Śikhaṇḍin, the great chariot-fighter, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa, and the unconquered Sātyaki.

[gita-a01-v18] The Pāñcāla great archer, the five Draupadeyas, and mighty-armed Saubhadra each blew conches separately.

[gita-a01-v19] That sound tore the hearts of Dhartarashtra's sons and resounded tumultuously through sky and earth.

[gita-a01-v20] Then, seeing Dhartarashtra's sons arrayed and weapons begun to clash, the monkey-bannered Pandava raised his bow.

[gita-a01-v21] Then Arjuna spoke this word to Hrishikesha: O lord of earth, place my chariot between both armies, O Acyuta.

[gita-a01-v22] Until I see these standing eager to fight, with whom by me must be fought in this battle effort.

[gita-a01-v23] I wish to see those who will fight, who are assembled here, desiring to please evil-minded Dhartarashtra in war.

[gita-a01-v24] Sanjaya said: thus addressed by Gudakesha, O Bharata, Hrishikesha placed the best chariot between both armies.

[gita-a01-v25] Arjuna said, O Partha, see these gathered Kurus led by Bhishma and Drona.

[gita-a01-v26] There Partha saw standing fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.

[gita-a01-v27] Fathers-in-law and friends were also in both armies.

[gita-a01-v28] Seeing all those kinsmen standing there, Arjuna was overcome by supreme compassion, sank down, and said this.

[gita-a01-v29] Arjuna said, seeing these kinsmen eager to fight, Krishna, my limbs sink and my mouth dries up.

[gita-a01-v30] Trembling and hair-standing arise in my body; Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns.

[gita-a01-v31] I cannot stand steady, my mind reels, and I see reversed omens, Keśava.

[gita-a01-v32] I see no good in slaying kin in battle; I do not desire victory, Kṛṣṇa, nor kingdom and pleasures.

[gita-a01-v33] What is kingdom to us, Govinda, or enjoyments and life, when those for whom we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures are to be slain?

[gita-a01-v34] Those standing in battle, abandoning lives and wealth, are teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers.

[gita-a01-v35] I do not wish to kill these kin, even for three-worlds sovereignty or earth; the opponent's view is stated before the answer.

[gita-a01-v36] Having slain the Dhartarashtrans, what joy would there be, O Janardana?

[gita-a01-v37] Sin would cling to us if we killed these aggressors; therefore we are not fit to kill our Dhārtarāṣṭra relatives. In such killing sin alone is the agent; our enemies are already subdued by sin, and killing them along with ourselves would bring sin. Here sin comes from greed and from failing to see faults such as the destruction of family.

[gita-a01-v38] Therefore Arjuna indeed raises the mention of duties such as family destruction: 'How, having killed our own people, could we be happy, O Madhava? Even if these men, their minds overcome by greed, do not see [the fault].'

[gita-a01-v39] How is the fault caused by the destruction of family, and the sin involved in treachery to friends, not to be known by us, so that we may turn away from sin?

[gita-a01-v40] O Janardana, those who clearly see the fault caused by the destruction of a family; when a family is destroyed, its eternal family duties perish.

[gita-a01-v41] When dharma is lost, the entire family is overcome by unrighteousness; and from that overcoming of unrighteousness, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt.

[gita-a01-v42] O Vārṣṇeya, when women are corrupted, varṇa-mixture arises; that mixture leads to hell for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself.

[gita-a01-v43] The ancestors fall because the rites of rice and water are lost, through the faults of family-destroyers who cause caste mixture.

[gita-a01-v44] Eternal birth-duties and family-duties are destroyed; for men whose family duties are destroyed, O Janardana, we have heard that dwelling in hell is certain.

[gita-a01-v45] Arjuna says it is a great sin to kill kinsmen out of desire for kingdom pleasure, expressing his own distress.

[gita-a01-v46] For the discerning one, withdrawal from war is fitting; being killed unarmed by weapon-handed Dhartarashtras in battle would be more beneficial.

[gita-a01-v47] Sanjaya said: having spoken thus in battle, Arjuna sat down in the chariot seat, casting aside bow and arrow, his mind distressed with grief.

[gita-a01-v48] Here is the summary verse: made helpless by the collision of knowledge and ignorance, abandoning both by reason, the sage without discernment becomes; thus in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, first chapter, one, thus auspicious.

[gita-a02-v01] Sanjaya says that Krishna, seeing Arjuna overcome with compassion and grief, spoke these words to him.

[gita-a02-v02] Krishna asks whence this faintness has come in difficulty, calling it unworthy, not heavenly, and fame-destroying, while first awakening Arjuna through worldly conduct.

[gita-a02-v03] Krishna shows that Arjuna's conceit of duty is unrighteous, forbids impotence, and commands him to abandon petty heart-weakness and rise.

[gita-a02-v04] Arjuna asks how he can fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, calling them worship-worthy.

[gita-a02-v05] Arjuna says it is better to live by begging than to kill great-souled teachers, and he would not enjoy blood-smeared pleasures after killing Bhishma and Drona.

[gita-a02-v06] Arjuna says he does not know which is better, that victory over relatives would be misfortune, and that he cannot decide whether to desire victory or defeat.

[gita-a02-v07] Overcome by the fault of poverty of spirit, with a mind confused about dharma, I ask you: declare what is certainly better; I am your surrendered disciple, instruct me.

[gita-a02-v08] I do not see what would remove my grief, even obtaining an unrivaled prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship even over the gods.

[gita-a02-v09] Sanjaya said: having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, scorcher of foes, said he would not fight; having spoken to Govinda, he became silent.

[gita-a02-v10] Hrishikesha said to him, smiling as it were, O Bharata: this sinking speech in the midst of both armies indicates that Arjuna, filled with doubt, is not withdrawn from battle on one side alone, because he says, instruct me, your surrendered one.

[gita-a02-v11] Therefore, standing between knowledge and ignorance, you are instructed by the holy Lord. The holy Lord said: your inner self is struck by humanity; overcome by grief and delusion, you are seized by pity; seeing kinsmen who have approached the mouth of death, what obstacle is yours? They have entered it themselves.

[gita-a02-v12] You grieve for what should not be grieved and do not speak like a wise person; learned ones do not grieve for the departed or the living. It is impossible to grieve for the body, since it is always perishable; and you grieve for the self, which is not worthy of grief. No one, whether dead or living, is to be grieved; for the self is indestructible, moving through various bodies, so what grief-worthiness is there? Nor is there grief-worthiness in the transfer of bodies; otherwise grief-worthiness would arise even in youth and so on.

[gita-a02-v13] Thus the two meanings are stated: I never was not, nor were you or these lords; we all shall be beyond this.

[gita-a02-v14] As the embodied self passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so it passes to another body; the steady one is not deluded.

[gita-a02-v15] Sense contacts through the senses produce impermanent states; endure them, Bharata.

[gita-a02-v16] The person whom these contacts do not disturb, steady in pain and pleasure, is fit for immortality.

[gita-a02-v17] Non-being has no being, and being has no non-being; truth-seers see the end of both.

[gita-a02-v18] Know that as indestructible by which all this is pervaded; no one can destroy the imperishable.

[gita-a02-v19] These bodies are finite, while the embodied self is eternal and immeasurable; therefore fight without grief.

[gita-a02-v20] The self neither slays nor is slain; one who thinks otherwise is ignorant and bound.

[gita-a02-v21] The self is unborn, eternal, and not slain when the body is slain.

[gita-a02-v22] One who knows the indestructible self neither slays nor is slain, so how is there bondage?

[gita-a02-v23] As worn garments are discarded and new ones taken, so the embodied self takes new bodies.

[gita-a02-v24] Weapons, fire, water, and wind do not destroy the self.

[gita-a02-v25] This Self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried; it is eternal, all-pervading, immovable, and everlasting.

[gita-a02-v26] This Self is unmanifest, inconceivable, and unmodifiable; therefore, having known it, one should not grieve. No weapon or other cause can destroy him, since he is of one conscious nature, independent, partless, and free, and cannot be destroyed by another nature, dependence, destruction of parts, or division. Nor is his going to another body something new: even while embodied he always goes to another body, and therefore he is connected. Since a body does not remain even for a moment, having known this Self thus, one should not grieve.

[gita-a02-v27] Even if you regard him as ever-born or dead, O mighty-armed, you should not grieve for him. Even if you regard the body as ever-born through an unbroken stream, there is no ground for grief through a momentary process; even if it is ever-perishing, what grief is there? Thus, if you think the self's union with or separation from that body makes it ever-born or ever-dead, grieving is in every way unfitting for knowers.

[gita-a02-v28] Since birth and death are inevitable and form a wheel, one should not grieve.

[gita-a02-v29] Since beings are unmanifest before and after, and change is only modification, there is no cause for lamentation.

[gita-a02-v30] The self is a wonder: some see it, some speak of it, some hear yet do not know it.

[gita-a02-v31] The embodied self is eternally indestructible in every body, Bharata; therefore you should not grieve for any beings, since the self's indestructibility is eternal.

[gita-a02-v32] Considering even your own duty, you should not waver; for a kshatriya no better righteous duty than war is found, and since own duty is non-removable, trembling about war is unfitting.

[gita-a02-v33] By chance such war arrives with heaven's gate opened; meritorious kshatriyas obtain it, Partha. Even desire-filled kshatriyas should not abandon such war because it causes heaven; how much less one to whom such knowledge is taught. The verse's purport is not merely ending in heaven.

[gita-a02-v34] The fear from which you would turn from war will itself fall upon you in a hundred branches. If you do not fight this righteous battle, then abandoning your own duty and fame you will obtain sin.

[gita-a02-v35] Beings will also speak your ill-fame; for an esteemed imperishable one, ill-fame surpasses death.

[gita-a02-v36] Great charioteers will think you retreated from battle out of fear; having been highly regarded by them, you will go to lightness in their eyes.

[gita-a02-v37] Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words and blame your power; what pain could be greater than that?

[gita-a02-v38] Slain, you gain heaven; victorious, you enjoy earth; therefore rise, son of Kunti, resolved for battle.

[gita-a02-v39] Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat equal, engage in battle; thus you will not incur sin.

[gita-a02-v40] This wisdom was told in Sankhya; hear how, endowed with it, you abandon action-bondage in yoga.

[gita-a02-v41] Even a little of this duty protects from great fear; even small yoga-wisdom destroys samsara-fear.

[gita-a02-v42] This wisdom is not newly brought; resolute wisdom is one, while unresolved wisdoms are many-branched and endless.

[gita-a02-v43] Thus fools speak this flowery speech, attached to Vedic debate, O Partha, claiming nothing else exists.

[gita-a02-v44] Desire-natured, heaven-focused, desiring fruits of birth and action, full of special rites, they follow paths toward enjoyment and power.

[gita-a02-v45] For minds stolen by that speech, resolute understanding is not given in concentration; desire-craving speakers praise flowery Vedic speech filled with future heaven-fruit, desire fruit from action, and even with resolute understanding are not fit for concentration because of fruit-certainty; this is the purport of the three verses.

[gita-a02-v46] Therefore the Vedas concern the three strands; be beyond them, Arjuna, beyond pairs, established in constant being, free from acquisition and security, self-possessed. The Vedas bind by three-stranded instrument especially, not as binders by nature, because Vedic actions done with pleasure-pain-delusion understanding are binding; therefore desire-form three-strandedness is to be abandoned. If this were Veda-criticism, the matter of doing battle would be obstructed, for lack of certainty of own duty without Veda; but for those whose desire for fruit has fallen away, the Vedas are not binders.

[gita-a02-v47] Because the Vedas are supreme for those fit for right knowing, therefore he says: as much purpose as in a well, so much in all Vedas for the knowing brahmin; for one whose primacy is in own duty and knowing, even limited Veda-spoken work is to be done.

[gita-a02-v48] Therefore your right is in action, never in fruits; do not be cause of action-fruit, and let no attachment be in inaction. Be engaged in action only, not in fruits. Surely action done necessarily brings fruit? Not so: if you are pervaded by fruit-desire impurity, then action becomes cause of fruit; unasked fruit is knowing, not for the unwilling. Attachment through absence of action is firm-grasp false knowing, to be abandoned indeed.

[gita-a02-v49] Established in yoga, do actions abandoning attachment; equality in success and failure is yoga.

[gita-a02-v50] One whose undertakings are free from desire-bonds is the wise renouncer; longing binds.

[gita-a02-v51] Action is far inferior to yoga of wisdom; seek refuge in intellect, for wretched fruit-causers remain distant.

[gita-a02-v52] Joined to intellect, one abandons both good and bad deeds; yoga is skill in actions.

[gita-a02-v53] Wise ones, abandoning action-born fruit, are freed from birth-bond and attain the unailing state.

[gita-a02-v54] When your intellect crosses the delusion-thicket, then you will go to weariness of what is to be heard and heard.

[gita-a02-v55] When your intellect stands unmoving in samadhi, you will attain yoga; then recognition becomes clear and dispassion follows.

[gita-a02-v56] Arjuna asks what speech, sitting, and going characterize steady wisdom in samadhi.

[gita-a02-v57] When one abandons all desires and is content in the self, steady wisdom is declared.

[gita-a02-v58] Unagitated in suffering, desireless in pleasure, free from attachment, fear, and anger, such a sage is steady-minded.

[gita-a02-v59] Fitting, because one unattached everywhere, obtaining good or bad, neither rejoices nor hates, and wisdom is established.

[gita-a02-v60] When one withdraws the senses from objects like a tortoise, steady wisdom is declared.

[gita-a02-v61] Objects withdraw from one who fasts, but taste remains; seeing the supreme removes that residue, so only the yogin is steady in wisdom.

[gita-a02-v62] Even a wise person's mind is seized by turbulent senses, so the yogin must conquer the mind.

[gita-a02-v63] Having restrained the senses by mind, one should sit devoted to me; wisdom is established when senses are controlled.

[gita-a02-v64] For one meditating on objects, attachment arises; from attachment desire, and from desire anger.

[gita-a02-v65] Anger leads to delusion, memory confusion, intellect destruction, and ruin; mere renunciation ends in grasping, so it is not the means for steady wisdom.

[gita-a02-v66] Freed from attachment and aversion, moving through objects with controlled senses, the self-controlled one attains serenity.

[gita-a02-v67] In calmness, loss of all sorrows arises for him; indeed quickly the intellect of the clear-minded one becomes established.

[gita-a02-v68] There is no intellect for the unyoked one, nor meditation for the unyoked one, nor peace for the unpeaceful one; whence happiness?

[gita-a02-v69] Indeed, of the roaming senses, the mind that follows them carries away his wisdom, as wind carries a boat on water.

[gita-a02-v70] Therefore, O mighty-armed one, whose senses are wholly restrained from sense-objects, his wisdom is established; but one who controls the mind, even while serving objects, is not overwhelmed by waves of anger and the like; thus he alone is the steady-wisdom yogi—this is the purport.

[gita-a02-v71] The yogi, though performing all practical dealings, is transcendent; the supreme Lord, having summarized his own nature, tells it: the night of all beings is the sage's waking; the night in which beings wake is the sage's night; how is this maya, the deluding night of all beings, to be abandoned? In the state where the world wakes and performs various activities, that is the sage's night, because he is unawakened to practical dealing. This is said: this maya indeed has deluding nature, name-and-form, and appearance of dependence on pleasure; there the world, without touching her original own-nature, sits bound in memory in the second form. The yogi, however, is opposite: he sees her deluding nature for uprooting it, and does not regard dependence on pleasure; seeing rightly, the knower disregards dependence on pleasure through destruction of false knowledge. See indeed, that is night—wonder! In knowledge the yogi attends where all are deluded; in ignorance, however, where a person is unawakened, there he is awakened—also wonder.

[gita-a02-v72] Therefore indeed, just as waters enter the ocean that is being filled yet remains immovably established, so all desires enter him; he attains peace, not the desire-desiring one. The yogi does not run outward even for desire's sake; but by sense-nature, objects entering after him do not make waves, like river currents into the ocean. Thus the third is decided.

[gita-a02-v73] Having abandoned all desires, the desireless, selfless, egoless man walks and attains peace; that yogi, through renunciation of all desires, reaches liberation in the form of peace.

[gita-a02-v74] This is the brahmic state, Partha; having reached it one is not deluded, and even at the end one reaches brahma-nirvana. This brahma-being, in which even a moment's stability, once obtained, leads from body-breaking to supreme brahman, is thus the resolution of the four questions; auspicious.

[gita-a02-v75] Here is the summary verse: ah, indeed the mind's wondrous course ascends by abandonment; taking refuge in objects, one should abandon them. Thus in the Gita-meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, the second chapter.

[gita-a03-v01] Now the third chapter: if your thought holds action superior, O Janardana, then why do you engage me in terrible action, O Kesava?

[gita-a03-v02] You seem to confuse my intelligence with mixed speech; speak one decided way by which I may attain the good.

[gita-a03-v03] The Lord gives a reply: in this world twofold steadfastness was formerly declared by me, O sinless one.

[gita-a03-v04] A person does not attain inaction by not beginning actions, nor does he attain perfection by renunciation alone.

[gita-a03-v05] No one ever stands without acting even for a moment; everyone is made to act helplessly by the gunas born of nature.

[gita-a03-v06] He who restrains the action organs yet remembers sense objects by mind is deluded and is called of foolish conduct.

[gita-a03-v07] One who restrains the senses by mind and begins action-yoga without attachment excels in actions; no knowledge is lost because action proceeds like a machine.

[gita-a03-v08] Therefore do prescribed action; action is better than inaction, and even body maintenance depends on action.

[gita-a03-v09] This world is bound by action other than sacrifice; therefore perform action for sacrifice, free from attachment, since obligatory action without fruit-attachment does not yield binding fruit.

[gita-a03-v10] Having created beings with sacrifice, the lord of beings said that through it they should procreate; beings were created together with actions, and actions yield either world-cycle through attachment or liberation through detachment.

[gita-a03-v11] Nourish the gods by this action, and they will nourish you; mutual nourishment of gods and senses quickly yields supreme welfare.

[gita-a03-v12] Gods nourished by sacrifice give desired objects; one who enjoys them without returning is a thief, so enjoyments should be used as they arise.

[gita-a03-v13] Those who eat the remainder of sacrifice are freed from all sins, while those who cook only for themselves obtain sin.

[gita-a03-v14] Beings arise from food, food from rain, rain from sacrifice, and sacrifice from action.

[gita-a03-v15] Know action as born from brahman and brahman from the imperishable; all-pervading brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.

[gita-a03-v16] One who does not follow this wheel lives in vain, and one who delights only in the senses is full of sin.

[gita-a03-v17] For a human who delights in the self and is self-satisfied, no duty remains.

[gita-a03-v18] For him no purpose arises from action or nonaction, and he acts without dependence on purpose in beings.

[gita-a03-v19] Janaka and others attained perfection through action; seeing world-welfare, you too should act, and they remain examples for those acting toward perfection.

[gita-a03-v20] Whatever the best person does, others do; whatever standard he sets, the world follows.

[gita-a03-v21] O Partha, I have no duty in the three worlds, nothing unattained to attain, yet I engage in action.

[gita-a03-v22] If I did not ever act unweariedly, people would follow my path in every way, O Partha.

[gita-a03-v23] These worlds would perish if I did not act; I would become maker of confusion and harm these beings.

[gita-a03-v24] Therefore, always perform duty unattached; for an unattached person performing action attains the supreme.

[gita-a03-v25] As the unwise act attached, the wise should act unattached for the gathering of the world.

[gita-a03-v26] The wise should not disturb the intellect of the ignorant, but engage all actions properly.

[gita-a03-v27] The deluded self thinks itself the doer and binds itself falsely.

[gita-a03-v28] Knowing the distinction of strands and action, one does not attach.

[gita-a03-v29] Deluded by nature's strands, people attach to actions; the united should engage in them.

[gita-a03-v30] Renouncing all actions to me, fight desireless and mineless for world grace.

[gita-a03-v31] Those faithful humans who always practice this teaching are freed from all actions; whoever relies on it and does anything is not bound.

[gita-a03-v32] Those who disparage and do not follow this teaching are deluded and lost; the unfaithful in this knowledge are destroyed continuously because of fear of birth and death.

[gita-a03-v33] Even the knower acts according to his own nature; beings go to nature and dissolve there, so what can restraint do? Even the knower shows no reversal in conduct such as eating, but acts fittingly; since beings dissolve in nature and the self is non-agent and eternally free, whose birth and so on can be restrained? How then is there bondage? Thus it is said.

[gita-a03-v34] For each sense in its object, attraction and aversion are established; one should not come under their sway, for they are obstacles to him.

[gita-a03-v35] One's own duty, though flawed, is better than another's well performed; death in one's own duty is better than another's arising. The world-bound one grasps attraction and aversion toward each object, regarding actions as self-performed through delusion. Even equally in eating and conduct, the knowing and world-bound differ. Our settled doctrine: for one freed from attachment and practicing own duty, no merit-demerit bondage exists, since own duty does not depart from the heart and is rooted in one's own nature; thus no creature is born empty, so it is not to be abandoned.

[gita-a03-v36] Arjuna asks by what impelled a person commits sin even unwillingly, as if forced, and how a person proceeds knowing it as sin. The question's arising has this intent: if own duty does not depart from the heart, how can unrighteous conduct be this? What is this own duty by which a creature is said to be empty? Here the answer: even though own duty is in the heart, this disturbance is made by a foreign covering, not by its absence.

[gita-a03-v37] Kṛṣṇa says desire and anger, born of rajas, are the great devourer and sin-giver; the wise should know this enemy.

[gita-a03-v38] Arjuna asks Kṛṣṇa how this enemy arises, grows, what it is, and what it does.

[gita-a03-v39] Kṛṣṇa says the enemy is subtle and supreme, deluding Pārtha through the senses, though truly sorrow and delusion.

[gita-a03-v40] Desire and anger become a terrible ego of pride and joy, hard to cross through sinful actions.

[gita-a03-v41] The enemy turns away joy, gives grief, makes fear, and deludes repeatedly; pride grows ego-nature through pleasure-thought.

[gita-a03-v42] The enemy is impure, fault-seeking, rajas-driven delusion that destroys this and other worlds by faults.

[gita-a03-v43] Just as fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so this self is covered by that. Through these three examples are said its hard-to-remove quality, its doing of forbidden acts, and its being a seat of disgust: this is the self.

[gita-a03-v44] Knowledge is covered by desire, the knower's eternal enemy, O Kaunteya—an insatiable fire that roams through the senses and burns both seen and unseen, never to be filled.

[gita-a03-v45] The senses, mind, and intellect are said to be the seat of the embodied being; through them he deludes the embodied one by covering knowledge. First, when the senses are present, it stands; just as an enemy seen by the eye generates anger in the sense-region itself, then in the mind's determination, then in the intellect's certainty; by this means, generating delusion, he destroys knowledge.

[gita-a03-v46] To prevent this evil, first restrain the senses, O best of Bharatas, and abandon the evil that destroys knowledge and realization; do not first grasp knowledge of Brahman, realization, or divine-filled action, since it destroys; therefore abandon anger; or, having prevented destruction by knowledge-mind and realization-intellect, do not grasp what arises in the senses as intention, nor determine the intended.

[gita-a03-v47] Here the method is stated in two verses: the senses are called superior; beyond the senses is the mind; beyond the mind is intelligence; and beyond intelligence is he.

[gita-a03-v48] Thus, having known what is beyond intellect and steadied oneself by oneself, slay the enemy, mighty-armed, formed of desire and hard to approach. The senses are other than sense-objects marked as enemy; mind is other than them; intellect is distinct even from mind; and the self is that whose nature is other. How can anger born of the senses agitate mind, intellect, or self? Thus consider. The intent of secret knowers is that intellect abides elsewhere; supreme ego is all-I identity-nature, supreme nonduality. Because the full has no fragmentation, anger and the rest do not arise. Therefore, grasping supreme ego—other-enthusiasm, consciousness-natured anger, ignorance-natured enemy—slay it; auspicious.

[gita-a03-v49] Here is the summary verse: what can anger and other mind-delusions do to one who regards wife, body, and dense things as other? Thus ends the third chapter of Abhinavagupta's Gita Meaning Gathering.

[gita-a04-v01] Now the fourth chapter: the Lord said, thus I taught the imperishable yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat spoke it to Manu, and Manu declared it to Ikshvaku.

[gita-a04-v02] Thus royal sages knew this tradition-received yoga, but it was lost in great time, scorcher of foes; and though obtained by teacher lineage, it is now lost; by this the Lord shows the rarity and weight of this knowledge.

[gita-a04-v03] That same ancient yoga has been taught to you today; you are my devotee and friend, and this highest secret is so; by the word ca a secondary sense is said, so devotion here is primary toward the teacher, not friendship; this is the purport. Arjuna, though knowing the Lord's own form, asks in the world to make it clear.

[gita-a04-v04] Arjuna said: your later birth and Vivasvat's earlier birth—how should I know this, that you taught at first?

[gita-a04-v05] The Lord said: many births of mine have passed, and yours too, Arjuna; I know all those, but you do not, scorcher of foes.

[gita-a04-v06] Though unborn and imperishable in self, though lord of beings, presiding over my own nature, I am born by my own maya.

[gita-a04-v07] When duty declines and unrighteousness rises, the Lord creates a self-portion and takes a body to sustain the world.

[gita-a04-v08] For protecting the good, destroying wrongdoers, and establishing duty, I manifest in every age.

[gita-a04-v09] Whoever truly knows my divine birth and action leaves the body without rebirth and comes to me.

[gita-a04-v10] Many, purified by knowledge and austerity and absorbed in me, attain my state while doing action without fruit.

[gita-a04-v11] As people surrender to me, so I worship them; all follow my path, and I take the form sought by devotees.

[gita-a04-v12] Those desiring success in action worship deities here; success born of action occurs quickly in the human world.

[gita-a04-v13] The fourfold order was created by me according to guna and karma; know me as maker yet non-doer and imperishable.

[gita-a04-v14] Actions do not stain me, nor is desire in fruits; one who knows this is not bound by actions.

[gita-a04-v15] Knowing this, do action as ancients did; purified by this intelligence, perform necessary actions.

[gita-a04-v16] Success is not from non-action alone; even poets are deluded here, so I will declare action by knowing which you are freed.

[gita-a04-v17] Action, forbidden action, and non-action must be known; the course of action is deep and hard to discern.

[gita-a04-v18] One who sees non-action in action and action in non-action is wise among humans.

[gita-a04-v19] Whose every undertaking is free from desire-intention, and whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge, him the wise call learned. Hence, abandoning intention regarding desired objects and fruits, actions that are performed enter the fire of knowledge, whose nature is described and to be described, and are burned.

[gita-a04-v20] Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content and without support, though engaged in action he does nothing at all; though eager and active, he does nothing.

[gita-a04-v21] A desireless person with controlled mind and self, having abandoned all possessions, does only bodily action; bodily action is that which is useful to the body and of the nature of sense activity, and it is not tinged by mind and intellect.

[gita-a04-v22] One who is content with what comes by chance, beyond opposites, free from envy, and equal in success and failure is not bound even while acting. Action binds the agent only by taking on the impurity of desire for fruit; the self binds itself. Otherwise, if inert actions themselves bound, freedom in bondage would not be heartfelt.

[gita-a04-v23] For one freed of attachment, liberated, mind resting in knowing, acting for sacrifice — all action melts away; and 'for sacrifice' is uttered in the singular, the sacrifices being those described hereafter.

[gita-a04-v24] The verse says sacrifice in its general nature is brahma offered into brahma-fire by brahma; through brahma-action concentration one goes to brahma. For one engaged, offering in brahma leads to re-entry there. The whole world-souled brahma is the oblation offered in supreme knowledge, in quiet fire, for the increase of radiance. For the yogi whose concentration is such brahma-action, brahma alone is to be gone to and known, and no other fruit is obtained. Limited sacrificers receive limited fruit, while knowers of unlimited complete self-sacrifice do not. The verse binds a supreme secret, explained according to intellect and teacher-tradition; some say instruments and action are brahma-qualifications, but that is to be neglected because the secret tradition-sequence remains unbroken.

[gita-a04-v25] Some yogis worship divine sacrifice, others offer sacrifice into brahma-fire, and others offer senses and objects; all obtain self-gain.

[gita-a04-v26] Some offer senses into restraint-fires, others offer objects into sense-fires; mind is the fire, and enjoyment is the identity of enjoyer and enjoyed.

[gita-a04-v27] Others offer all sense-actions and breath-actions into the self-restraint yoga-fire illuminated by knowledge.

[gita-a04-v28] Substance, austerity, yoga, self-study, and knowledge sacrifices are named; ascetics offer mental and breath activities into the one-pointed fire illuminated by knowledge.

[gita-a04-v29] Some offer prana into apana and apana into prana; restraining both movements, they are devoted to breath-control.

[gita-a04-v30] Others with regulated food offer breaths into breaths; all sacrifice-knowers have sins destroyed, and prana rises as sound ending in om, distinguishing self-study and knowledge sacrifices.

[gita-a04-v31] Those who eat the nectar left from sacrifice go to eternal brahman; without sacrifice there is no world, and sacrifice nourishes the faculties while leaving self-rest.

[gita-a04-v32] Many sacrifices spread from brahman's mouth; knowing them as means, one is freed from bondage.

[gita-a04-v33] Knowledge-sacrifice is better than material sacrifice, because all action is completed in knowledge.

[gita-a04-v34] Know that through prostration, questioning, and service, reality-seers teach knowledge.

[gita-a04-v35] Knowing this, you will not again fall into delusion; you will see all beings in yourself and in me.

[gita-a04-v36] Even if you are the greatest sinner among all sinners, you will cross all sin by the raft of knowledge.

[gita-a04-v37] As a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.

[gita-a04-v38] Nothing here is as pure as knowledge; the yogin perfected by yoga finds it in the self in time.

[gita-a04-v39] The faithful, intent on that, with restrained senses, obtains knowledge; having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace.

[gita-a04-v40] The ignorant, faithless, doubting self perishes; there is no world, other world, or happiness for the doubting self. Knowledge-fire arises through practice-born certainty, and nothing equals knowledge in purity.

[gita-a04-v41] Actions do not bind the self-possessed one who has renounced actions by yoga and cut doubt by knowledge; renunciation of actions comes through yoga alone.

[gita-a04-v42] Therefore, having cut with the sword of knowledge the doubt born of ignorance and seated in the heart, stand in yoga and arise, O Bhārata.

[gita-a04-v43] Here the summary verse declares that action preceded by mere desire alone satisfies the good-possessing sense-powers divinities.

[gita-a05-v01] Now the fifth chapter. Arjuna said: O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and again yoga; tell me decisively which one of these two is better. The question of the doubtful one is: is renunciation primary, or yoga again?

[gita-a05-v02] The blessed Lord said: Renunciation and action-yoga are both bestowers of the highest good; but of the two, action-yoga is superior to renunciation of action. Here renunciation and action are not declared as one; rather, both combined give the highest good. Without yoga, renunciation does not arise; such is the distinction of yoga.

[gita-a05-v03] The one to be known is the eternal renouncer who neither hates nor desires; free from opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily released from bondage. Therefore he alone is the renouncer for all time, by whom desire and aversion of mind are renounced, because his intellect has gone beyond pairs such as anger and delusion; he is indeed easily freed.

[gita-a05-v04] Fools call sankhya and yoga separate, but the wise do not; one who abides rightly obtains the fruit of both.

[gita-a05-v05] What sankhya attains yoga also reaches; one who sees both sees rightly, for these two are eternally connected and neither knowing nor yoga stands without the other.

[gita-a05-v06] Renunciation is hard without yoga, but a yoga-united sage attains brahman without delay; for yogis this is easily obtained, while without yoga it is painful.

[gita-a05-v07] Even while acting, one who is yoked to yoga, pure in self, master of self and senses, and whose self has become the self of all beings is not stained; likewise one whose self is the self of all beings, even while doing everything, is not stained, because of the elevated denial of the instruments of action.

[gita-a05-v08] The knower of truth, though yoked, would not think, 'I do nothing at all,' while perceiving, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, breathing, and sleeping.

[gita-a05-v09] Speaking, releasing, grasping, opening, and closing—even so, the senses function among sense-objects; holding thus.

[gita-a05-v10] One who places actions in Brahman and abandons attachment is not stained by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water; therefore, even while performing acts such as seeing, one remains firm in realization, recognizes that the senses' activity in their own objects brings no personal result, and understands that another's deed does not stain another. Offering actions to Brahman is the sign of freedom from attachment, and so one is not stained.

[gita-a05-v11] Yogis perform actions through body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, having abandoned attachment for self-purification; and because attachment is absent, they act through these instruments as mutually independent and free from attachment.

[gita-a05-v12] The disciplined person, abandoning the fruit of action, attains final peace; the undisciplined person, acting from desire and attached to the fruit, is bound and does not return.

[gita-a05-v13] Renouncing all actions by mind, the controlled embodied one sits happily in the nine-gated city, not acting or causing, just as a man inside a house is not affected by those in the house.

[gita-a05-v14] The lord does not create agency, actions, or union with fruit; nature proceeds. The self does nothing for anyone; its activity is only nature, not desire for fruit.

[gita-a05-v15] The all-pervading lord takes no sin or merit; knowledge covered by ignorance deludes beings, and sin is done by their own ignorance.

[gita-a05-v16] By knowledge ignorance is destroyed; knowledge then manifests the supreme, self-manifest like the sun when darkness is gone.

[gita-a05-v17] Those whose intellect and self are fixed there, devoted and focused, go to non-return, purified by knowledge from stain.

[gita-a05-v18] Even remembering and touching this, though attached in their own action, they do not stick in mud, like sun rays, because nature proceeds thus.

[gita-a05-v19] The wise see equally in brahmin, cow, elephant, dog, and outcaste, yet act appropriately; consciousness-nature is one in all bodies.

[gita-a05-v20] The steady, unconfused knower of brahman does not rejoice or grieve at gain; friend-enemy distinction is only convention.

[gita-a05-v21] The self unattached to external contacts finds happiness in itself and enjoys imperishable happiness through brahman-yoga.

[gita-a05-v22] Contact-born enjoyments are pain-sources with beginning and end; the wise one does not delight in them.

[gita-a05-v23] He who can endure the impulse of desire and anger before bodily release is disciplined and happy.

[gita-a05-v24] He who is happy within, delighted within, and inner light attains supreme yoga as brahman-become.

[gita-a05-v25] Sages obtain brahmanirvāṇa when their stains are worn away, duality is cut, selves are restrained, they are devoted to the welfare of all beings, and the two knots of difference and doubt are destroyed.

[gita-a05-v26] For ascetics freed from desire and anger, with controlled minds and known selves, brahmanirvāṇa is present on all sides; the ultimate existence of brahman in every state does not await a time of cessation.

[gita-a05-v27] Having made contacts external and kept the eye within, one equalizes prāṇa and apāna, arranges all senses, establishes mind-activity in equality, and does not act crookedly; this alone is external.

[gita-a05-v28] A sage with restrained senses, mind, and intellect, devoted to liberation, whose desire, fear, and anger have departed, is always liberated; such a yogin, even while conducting all transactions, is indeed liberated.

[gita-a05-v29] Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, great lord of all worlds, and friend of all beings, one attains peace; knowing such divine principle, one is liberated even while situated as is.

[gita-a05-v30] Here is the summary verse: for one who sees all beings with equality, even conduct like the inert serves only for liberation.

[gita-a06-v01] The lord said: one who does duty as action without relying on its fruit is both renouncer and yogi, not one who merely abandons fire or action.

[gita-a06-v02] What is called renunciation is yoga; know this, pandava. No one becomes a yogi without renounced resolve, and renunciation without yoga does not arise.

[gita-a06-v03] Even so, for the sage ascending to yoga action is called the cause, while for the one established in yoga calm itself is called the cause.

[gita-a06-v04] When one does not cling to sense objects or actions, that renouncer of all resolves is called established in yoga.

[gita-a06-v05] One should lift oneself by oneself and not degrade oneself; the self is indeed friend and enemy of itself.

[gita-a06-v06] For one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is friend; for the unconquered, the self remains like an enemy.

[gita-a06-v07] For one who has conquered the self, the tranquil — toward higher and lower selves there is same-mindedness; in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, likewise in honor and dishonor; tranquil, free of ego, with nondual mind unnegated, without attraction and aversion.

[gita-a06-v08] A yogi is one whose self is satisfied by knowledge and realization, firm-standing, sense-conquered, yoked, and equal to clod, stone, and gold; unerring knowledge is intellect, and where there is various knowledge, that realization is the action previously spoken.

[gita-a06-v09] Equal-mindedness excels among friends, allies, enemies, neutrals, mediators, saints, and sinners; one who is thus equal-minded gradually excels and crosses samsara.

[gita-a06-v10] Here creation is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality; Brahman is faultless and equal, so they are established in Brahman. Even while connected to the body, creation is conquered through equality, and for them samsara is non-binding, since they are established in equality, and equality itself is Brahman.

[gita-a06-v11] The verse teaches that a yogi seeking ascent should constantly practice in solitude, controlling mind and self, remaining desireless and unpossessive, and making mind and self one-pointed; this is to be done under the proper conditions, not for a limited time.

[gita-a06-v12] Having established a firm seat for oneself in a pure place—not too high and not too low—with cloth, deer skin, and kuśa grass on top.

[gita-a06-v13] Making the mind one-pointed there, with restrained mind, senses, and actions, sitting on a seat, one should practice yoga for self-purification; by steadiness of seat and time, mind-steadiness arises, and mind-actions and other sense-actions are led into restraint.

[gita-a06-v14] Holding body, head, and neck even and motionless, steady, looking at the tip of one's own nose, and not looking at the directions.

[gita-a06-v15] With calm self, fearless in the celibacy vow, established, having restrained the mind, mind fixed on me, joined, one should sit, devoted to me; holding with effort in looking at the nose tip, not looking at directions, with mind fixed on me, joined, one should sit, thus the meaning.

[gita-a06-v16] Thus uniting the self, my devotee with undivided mind attains supreme liberation and my abode; for one who so unites the self, peace arises, in which the final limit of abode is found, and my attainment-yoga exists.

[gita-a06-v17] Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who fasts one-sidedly, nor for one who sleeps too much, nor for one who stays awake too much, Arjuna.

[gita-a06-v18] For one moderate in food and recreation, moderate in effort in actions, and moderate in sleep and waking, yoga becomes pain-removing.

[gita-a06-v19] When the restrained mind abides in the self alone, desireless toward all desires, the yogi is called yoked.

[gita-a06-v20] As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so the yogi's controlled mind does not move; objects and efforts are its movement.

[gita-a06-v21] Where the mind ceases through yoga practice, and the self sees itself in the self, there it is satisfied.

[gita-a06-v22] That supreme bliss, beyond the senses and grasped by intellect, is known where one, standing, does not move in truth.

[gita-a06-v23] Having obtained it, one considers no other gain greater; standing in it, one is not shaken even by heavy suffering.

[gita-a06-v24] Know that as yoga, separation from union with suffering; it must be practiced with certainty by an unwearied mind.

[gita-a06-v25] Abandoning all desires born of resolve, one restrains the whole sense-group by mind on every side.

[gita-a06-v26] Slowly withdraw by intellect held in firmness, making the mind self-abiding; think nothing at all, thinning desire-sorrow gradually, and do not accept mere object-cessation as the goal.

[gita-a06-v27] Wherever the unsteady mind goes out, restrain it and lead it to calm in the self; otherwise the unstable mind again clings to objects.

[gita-a06-v28] Supreme happiness approaches the calm-minded yogi who has become brahman and stainless.

[gita-a06-v29] Thus uniting the self, the yogi with controlled mind attains ultimate union with brahman with ease.

[gita-a06-v30] The yoga-united self sees the self abiding in all beings and all beings in the self; contemplating the self entering as knower unifies all beings, so equal seeing arises.

[gita-a06-v31] Whoever sees me everywhere and sees all things in me is not lost to me, nor am I lost to him. Destruction comes from non-action. The all-pervading form of the supreme self flees from one who does not see it, since its own form is not manifested. All things are established in the supreme self, the self-illuminator. One who does not see this is lost from true nature, apart from true shining. But one who sees me all-pervading is not lost to me by my own form, through shining; and fears seen in me fit that shining when seership is complete, so such a one is not lost of the supreme self.

[gita-a06-v32] He who, established in unity, worships me as present in all beings abides in me though acting in every way; and he who is filled with knowledge, knowing the all-pervading Lord through oneness, is not tainted though he has passed through all states.

[gita-a06-v33] He who sees everywhere equally by self-likeness, Arjuna, whether pleasure or pain, is considered the supreme yogi; and he sees the pleasure and pain of all as equal to himself. Thus this nature is declared; it is not again a new rule.

[gita-a06-v34] Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this yoga of equanimity that you have declared, I do not see its firm stability because of fickleness.

[gita-a06-v35] O Krishna, the mind is unsteady, agitating, strong, and firm; I consider restraining it very difficult, like the wind. Though Brahman is indicated, even clearly and directly, by the sequence of means declared by the Lord through indirect and direct indicators, it remains far away because of the mind's unsteadiness and badness; thus made indirect, it agitates, powerful in seen and unseen matters, and cannot be restrained from firm evil activity. Here is the answer.

[gita-a06-v36] The blessed Lord said: Without doubt, O mighty-armed one, the mind is hard to restrain and restless; yet by practice and by detachment it is grasped. By detachment, eagerness for objects is destroyed; by practice, the side of liberation is progressively made an object. Thus the taking up of both is stated; and there, by you, the commentator says restraint of mind-modifications depends on both—though the final token remains unclear.

[gita-a06-v37] Yoga is hard for an uncontrolled self, but attainable by a controlled, striving self through practice and prescribed means.

[gita-a06-v38] Arjuna asks about one endowed with faith whose mind has deviated from yoga and who is confused on the path of brahman.

[gita-a06-v39] Arjuna asks what course one takes who, confused and deluded, fails to attain yoga perfection, noting that faith may remain even if the mind deviates.

[gita-a06-v40] Arjuna asks whether one who loses both yoga and brahman perishes like a cut cloud or attains destruction.

[gita-a06-v41] Arjuna asks Krishna to cut his doubt completely, since no one else can resolve whether a failed yogi perishes or remains unestablished.

[gita-a06-v42] Krishna says there is no destruction for such a person in this world or the next, because a doer of good never goes to a bad course and faith is not lost.

[gita-a06-v43] Having attained and dwelt for eternal years in meritorious worlds, the one fallen from yoga is born in the house of pure and prosperous people; there are three eternal Vaishnava years of eternal Vishnu; this concerns those called pure whose minds touch a portion of the divine.

[gita-a06-v44] Or, such a birth arises only in the family of wise yogis; indeed this birth is rarer in the world. But if there must be gradation in its release, then it arises indeed in a yogi family. Thus it is said: this is rarer indeed. In the house of the prosperous, surely obstacles necessarily exist in accomplishment of liberation.

[gita-a06-v45] There he regains the intelligence-connection of his former life; then he strives again for perfection, O son of Kuru.

[gita-a06-v46] By previous practice one is carried even unwilling; even one desiring to know yoga transcends word-Brahman. Indeed, even unwilling and dependent, by that previous practice alone one is forcibly led to yoga practice. This is not ordinary: mere inquiry into yoga alone does not transcend word-Brahman; word-Brahman in the form of mantra-study and the like is not transcended but taken up.

[gita-a06-v47] A yogi who strives earnestly, is purified of sin, and perfected through many births goes to the supreme goal; after inquiry and diligent practice he attains Vasudeva-state at death, not by that body alone but through many births of practice; one whose sole occupation is devotion to divine activity is to be judged fallen from yoga, declaring yoga's preeminence.

[gita-a06-v48] The yogi is greater than ascetics, knowers, and workers; therefore, Arjuna, be a yogi. His superiority to ascetics was already shown; to knowers, because knowledge is yoga's fruit; to workers, because he knows what actions to do, and mere strenuous yoga without the Lord is not said to bring perfection.

[gita-a06-v49] Among all yogins, the faithful one who worships the Lord with inner self turned toward Him is considered most united; he places the Lord in the inner organ, is devoted to devotion and faith, and by the tradition-order obtained through service to the guru's feet worships and reflects on the Lord alone, not another; he is most united, entered into the supreme Lord. Thus the supremacy of all knowing with the Lord is declared. Auspicious. 49.

[gita-a06-v50] Here is the summary verse: all is obtained by mere attainment of the Lord's name, as rice plants ripen when proper rain alone is seen. 6. Thus in the gathering of the meaning of the holy Bhagavad Gita, composed by the feet of Abhinavagupta, the sixth chapter. 6.

[gita-a07-v01] Now the seventh chapter: the blessed Lord said, O Pārtha, with mind fixed in me, practicing yoga while taking refuge in me, you will know me wholly without doubt; hear that.

[gita-a07-v02] I will speak to you this knowledge with direct knowledge completely; having known it, nothing remains to be known, since in knowledge and action nothing of the knowable remains, because of fixity in knowledge and action.

[gita-a07-v03] Among thousands of men someone strives for perfection; among strivers and accomplished ones someone knows me in truth. By this, all are not fit for this thing, because of its rarity; effort-worthy knowledge is declared.

[gita-a07-v04] Earth, water, fire, wind, space, mind, intellect indeed, and ego: thus this divided nature of mine is eightfold.

[gita-a07-v05] Know my other superior nature, O mighty-armed, the living being by which this world is sustained; that which is seen by all people in the worldly state is one only, yet divided into eight modes; thus nonduality is shown even in nature-discussion, and she, having obtained livingness and personhood, is my superior nature, not another's, with both forms, varied manifold arrangement of knowable and knower, and from that indeed nature is the ground of all being, own-nature essence, always unfailing; this world-earth etc.

[gita-a07-v06] Ascertain that all beings have this as womb; I am the source and likewise dissolution of the whole world; do thus, and you indeed ascertain that I, become Vāsudeva, am source and dissolution of all; by this, the Lord is not different from nature, person, and supreme person, situated in every way by all-pervadingness; thus no difference-doctrine between Sāṃkhya and yoga is shown.

[gita-a07-v07] Nothing is higher than me; all this is strung in me like gems on a thread; though formless, I stand within all.

[gita-a07-v08] I am taste in waters, light in moon and sun, om in all Vedas, sound in space, and vigor in men.

[gita-a07-v09] I am pure smell in earth, radiance in fire, life in all beings, and austerity in ascetics.

[gita-a07-v10] Know me as the eternal seed of all beings; I am intelligence of the intelligent and radiance of the radiant.

[gita-a07-v11] I am strength free from desire and attachment, and desire not opposed to duty in beings.

[gita-a07-v12] Sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic states are from me; know them, but I am not in them; they are in me.

[gita-a07-v13] The world is deluded by strand-born states and does not know the supreme imperishable Lord; knowing alone reaches the Lord-principle.

[gita-a07-v14] Divine maya is hard to cross, yet those who resort to the Lord cross it; knowing supreme Brahman sees the world undivided.

[gita-a07-v15] Evil-doers, deluded and lowest, do not resort to the Lord because maya steals their knowledge.

[gita-a07-v16] Four kinds of well-doers worship the Lord: the distressed, the seeker, the wealth-seeker, and the knower.

[gita-a07-v17] Among them the knower, ever united, excels in single devotion; the knower is exceedingly dear to the Lord.

[gita-a07-v18] All these devotees are noble, yet the knower is esteemed as the Lord's own self, established in the supreme goal.

[gita-a07-v19] After many births the knower resorts to the Lord as all; such a great soul is rare, while other devotees are noble yet seek limited ends, and the knower alone rests in nondifference.

[gita-a07-v20] Those whose knowledge is stolen by desires resort to other deities, following rules determined by their own nature.

[gita-a07-v21] Whoever wishes to worship a form with faith, the Lord grants that very unwavering faith.

[gita-a07-v22] Endowed with that faith, he seeks worship of that form and obtains desires ordained by the Lord for his benefit.

[gita-a07-v23] The fruit of those worshippers is perishable, while my devotees go to me; limited desire-bound worship yields limited fruit.

[gita-a07-v24] The foolish think the unmanifest has become manifest and do not recognize the Lord's supreme imperishable form; they know only a form suited to their own desire.

[gita-a07-v25] I am not manifest to all, being covered by yoga-maya; this foolish world does not know me, the unborn and imperishable.

[gita-a07-v26] I know past, present, and future beings, Arjuna, but no one knows me; I do not come within the range of all. The doubt begins: do actions at dissolution grant liberation, otherwise why does great dissolution arise?

[gita-a07-v27] Born of desire and hatred, all beings enter pair-delusion at creation, O Bharata; that delusion expands, and the whole world, capable only of its own action-organs, takes on a sleep-like state, not ended merely by that much experience.

[gita-a07-v28] Those people whose sin has come to an end, doers of meritorious action, freed from pair-delusion, worship me with firm vows.

[gita-a07-v29] Those who strive, resorting to me, for liberation from old age and death know that brahman, all inner action, and everything; but those whose darkness is destroyed know brahman as all, studded with the Lord's rays, a stream of darkness of old age and death.

[gita-a07-v30] Those who know me with adhibhuta and adhidaiva, and with adhiyajna, know me even at departure with united mind; they know my other forms as inner, elemental, divine, and sacrificial. Because their inner organ is always filled with the Lord, they know me; from which, those whose Lord-principle is known even before birth would remember the supreme Lord at the end. What of birth-service? Those who think so, silence itself is auspicious. Thus auspicious.

[gita-a07-v31] Here is the summary verse: clearly, the Lord's devotion-devoid wish-fulfilling cluster, suitable to the practitioner's wish, may fulfill desires; thus, in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, the seventh chapter, seven.

[gita-a08-v01] Now the eighth chapter. Arjuna said: What is that Brahman? What is the self? What is action, O supreme person? What is said to be concerning beings? And what is called the divine?

[gita-a08-v02] How is the supreme sacrifice, and who is here in this body, O Madhusūdana? At the time of departure, how are you knowable by those of controlled selves? They know Brahman and so forth. By such questions raised by the Lord, preceded by nine questions, the matter is determined. The remainder is: how does the supreme sacrifice stand in the body?

[gita-a08-v03] The blessed Lord said: the supreme imperishable Brahman, whose own nature is called the inner self, is emission named action, causing the birth of beings' states; because of its greatness and expansion it is denoted by the word inner self; consciousness-being, whose nature is unceasing dharma, is Brahman unlimited externally, and through sovereign freedom embracing world-power it manifests external and inner-external being; that emission gradually causes the birth of beings from Brahma-knowers to inert things, manifesting inert and non-inert variety, and also makes the birth of truth when the false world of being is dissolved.

[gita-a08-v04] The perishable is the realm of beings; the person is the divine ground of all gods; and I alone am the sacrifice-overlord here in the body, best of embodied beings. Thus two questions are settled at once, while the remaining question is how you are to be known at the time of departure.

[gita-a08-v05] At the time of death, whoever remembers me alone and leaves the body goes to my state; there is no doubt about this.

[gita-a08-v06] Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body at death, that is the state one attains, O Kaunteya, being always imbued with that state.

[gita-a08-v07] Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight, with mind and intellect offered to Me; you will reach Me without doubt. This is not limited to a stable condition, but applies even at death, since constant cultivation of the Lord's nature brings remembrance of Him then.

[gita-a08-v08] By yoga of practice, with a mind that does not wander elsewhere, one reaches the supreme divine Person, O Partha, by thinking of him; after the body breaks, freed from bodily pain, one then thinks of the Lord.

[gita-a08-v09] He who remembers the seer, the ancient orderer, subtler than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, sun-colored, beyond darkness.

[gita-a08-v10] At the time of departure, with steady mind and devotion, endowed with yoga power, having properly fixed the breath between the eyebrows, he attains that supreme divine person. Thus one should remember: the Vasudeva principle is sun-colored, transcending the darkness of delusion, likened to the sun; between the eyebrows, as before.

[gita-a08-v11] That imperishable which the knowers of the Veda speak of, which ascetics free from attachment enter, and desiring which they practice brahmacarya—I will declare that state to you in summary; rightly grasped and determined by this, summary is the means; by that means I will declare that state here; for constant practice I will speak.

[gita-a08-v12] Having restrained all the senses, blocked the mind in the heart, and established the breath—self's charioteer—in the crown beyond all principles by will-power, one practices yoga concentration; this is bodily discipline, where 'in the heart' means freedom from attachment to sense objects rather than mere abiding in a bodily station.

[gita-a08-v13] He who departs uttering Om, the single syllable Brahman, remembering me, goes to the supreme goal.

[gita-a08-v14] The single-minded yogi who constantly remembers the Lord is easily attained by him; departure is not the decisive factor.

[gita-a08-v15] Having attained me, great souls do not return to the impermanent abode of suffering; elsewhere return remains.

[gita-a08-v16] All worlds up to Brahma return; attaining the Lord, there is no rebirth.

[gita-a08-v17] They know Brahma's day as a thousand yugas and night as a thousand yugas.

[gita-a08-v18] All manifest beings arise from the unmanifest at day and dissolve into the unmanifest at night.

[gita-a08-v19] The host of beings repeatedly arises and dissolves; the same living beings recur, with time making the difference of long or short cognition, and return is from everywhere except reaching the Lord.

[gita-a08-v20] Beyond that is another eternal being, manifest and unmanifest, which does not perish when all beings perish.

[gita-a08-v21] The unmanifest imperishable is called the supreme goal; reaching it there is no return, and that supreme abode is mine.

[gita-a08-v22] The supreme person is attainable by unwavering devotion; reaching him there is no rebirth, beings stand within him, and a distinction is stated for those desiring enjoyment.

[gita-a08-v23] Departing yogis go to non-return or return; the time for this will be spoken, non-return being liberation and return being for enjoyment.

[gita-a08-v24] Departing knowers of brahman in the bright six-month northern course go to brahman.

[gita-a08-v25] Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern course mark the path by which the yogi reaches lunar light and returns; the opposite northern course is light-natured and leads to non-return.

[gita-a08-v26] These white and black paths are the world's eternal courses; by one one goes to non-return, by the other one returns for enjoyment.

[gita-a08-v27] No knowing yogi is deluded by these paths; therefore be yoga-joined in all times, Arjuna.

[gita-a08-v28] Knowing all declared merit, the yogi reaches the supreme place and, through remembrance of the Lord, easily finds supreme Shiva.

[gita-a08-v29] Here is the summary verse: when all principles are known in the supreme Lord, there is no inside-or-outside condition in which the all-pervading shines.

[gita-a09-v01] Now the ninth chapter. The blessed Lord said: I will declare to the non-envious this most secret knowledge together with realized knowledge; knowing it, you will be freed from the inauspicious. Non-enviousness is the chief cause in the transmission of knowledge, as before in knowledge and realization.

[gita-a09-v02] This royal, secret, pure, supreme knowledge is directly perceived, righteous, easy to do, and imperishable; it shines among all knowledges and is called self-knowledge. Kings such as Janaka have authority in it; because it is greatly hidden it is secret, and because of heroic kshatriya steadiness it is very easy to do and perform; and its brahma-worship action entails no expenditure like other actions through enjoyment.

[gita-a09-v03] Men without faith in this dharma, O scorcher of foes, do not attain me; they turn back on the path of death and saṃsāra, being born again and again and dying.

[gita-a09-v04] I pervade this whole world in unmanifest form; all beings stand in me, yet I am not situated in them. Even considering for long that all beings stand in me, there is no other support-abode; in their appearance, the opposite knowledge-nature is concealed by making inert form preceded by the known self-nature. Thus it is said: I am not situated in them.

[gita-a09-v05] Beings do not dwell in me; see my divine yoga. I bear beings, yet my self, though sustaining beings, does not dwell in them. The ignorant, blind to truth, think the supreme Lord is limited, seeing only a finite self on earth; but the Lord's yoga is unsurpassed sovereign freedom.

[gita-a09-v06] Just as the great, all-pervading wind ever abides in space, so know that all beings abide in me.

[gita-a09-v07] Thus indeed I move unseen in all beings, resting on being-nature, together and without; as space and wind remain inseparable yet sky is never touched, so the Lord's principle, though spread through all world, is not an object for everyone.

[gita-a09-v08] All beings, son of Kunti, go to my nature at world-dissolution; again at world-beginning I emit those beings into unmanifest nature.

[gita-a09-v09] Taking hold of my own nature, I emit again and again this entire helpless group of beings by nature's control; by this much, even this inert group of beings has obtained manifestness through connection with the higher nature.

[gita-a09-v10] Those actions do not bind me, wealth-winner, seated like an indifferent one, unattached in those actions.

[gita-a09-v11] With me as overseer, nature produces moving and still things; by this cause, son of Kunti, the world revolves. There is no action-bondage for me by indifference, because I exist; therefore I am cause in world-creation without relying on activity.

[gita-a09-v12] Fools despise me dwelling in human body, not knowing the supreme imperishable being; I lie within all people, yet the Lord beyond the fourteen kinds, including human, is not found, so how does he exist?

[gita-a09-v13] Those of demonic and rakshasic nature have vain hopes, actions, and knowledge; their karma, knowledge, and desire are fruitless because directed to non-reality.

[gita-a09-v14] Great souls, resorting to divine nature, worship with unwavering mind, knowing the imperishable origin of beings.

[gita-a09-v15] Always glorifying, striving, vowed, bowing, and ever united, they worship with devotion.

[gita-a09-v16] Some worship by knowledge-sacrifice as one, others by external offerings in many ways; all are devoted to the Lord.

[gita-a09-v17] I am sacrifice, svadha, medicine, mantra, ghee, fire, and offering.

[gita-a09-v18] I am father, mother, supporter, and grandfather of this world; I am the knowable, purifier, om, rig, sama, and yajur.

[gita-a09-v19] The Lord is the goal, supporter, witness, dwelling, refuge, friend, origin, dissolution, abode, treasure, and imperishable seed.

[gita-a09-v20] The Lord heats, withholds, and releases; is nectar and death, being and nonbeing; one partless principle supports all action.

[gita-a09-v21] Knowers of the three Vedas, purified of sin, sacrifice and seek heaven; gaining merit, they enjoy divine pleasures in Indra's world.

[gita-a09-v22] They enjoy vast heaven, then return to the mortal world when merit is exhausted; desire limits the fruit, so they come and go.

[gita-a09-v23] For those who worship without other thought, the Lord carries yoga and security; yoga is gaining one's own form, security is protecting gained divine form.

[gita-a09-v24] Even devotees of other gods, endowed with faith, sacrifice; they too worship me, Kaunteya, though without proper rule.

[gita-a09-v25] I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices, yet they do not know me truly and therefore deviate.

[gita-a09-v26] God-vowed go to gods, ancestor-vowed to ancestors, being-worshippers to beings, and my worshippers to me.

[gita-a09-v27] Offerings made with devotion are accepted, and even worship under other names reaches me, since nothing worshippable exists apart from brahman; the difference lies in proper or improper rite.

[gita-a09-v28] Thus, one who knows in the stated order finds even an offering to Indra and other gods to be an offering to the supreme lord; every other action too becomes worship of the great lord as one's own self. Therefore whatever you do, eat, offer, give, or practice as austerity, O son of Kunti, do that as an offering to me.

[gita-a09-v29] Thus you will be freed from the bonds of action by auspicious and inauspicious fruits; united with renunciation-yoga and freed, you will approach me. Worshippers of other gods have limited desires and diminish the fruit; therefore you, by the previously stated teaching order, do contemplation as offering to me, as me-ness. This indeed is renunciation-yoga, already stated extensively and almost clearly before.

[gita-a09-v30] I am equal among all beings; to me none is hateful, none dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.

[gita-a09-v31] Even if someone is of very bad conduct, if he worships me with undivided devotion, he should indeed be considered a saint, for he is rightly resolved.

[gita-a09-v32] Quickly one becomes righteous and attains eternal peace; O son of Kunti, declare that my devotee does not perish. I declare it. Because the Lord has declared it, this reasoned meaning becomes firmly established.

[gita-a09-v33] O Partha, even those of sinful birth, women, vaishyas, and shudras who take refuge in me indeed go to the supreme destination.

[gita-a09-v34] How much more so holy brahmins and devoted royal sages; having obtained this impermanent, unhappy world, worship me.

[gita-a09-v35] Fix your mind on me, become my devotee and worshipper, bow to me, and you will come to me alone. Even those born in sinful wombs, animals, birds, reptiles, women, vaiśyas, śūdras, and dependent persons who take refuge in me worship me alone. The supremely compassionate Lord's deeds, such as the liberation of the elephant king, are heard in thousands. Some interpret the verse as praise of twice-born and kṣatriyas, not as an intent of liberation for women and others; they fragment the Lord's all-gracious power and cannot endure His supreme compassion. The Lord has no enemy and no dear one, even one of evil conduct. Other clear statements are contradicted by those who forcibly introduce difference into the nondual essence of the Lord and ignore scriptural contradictions. When questioned, those deeply immersed in caste obsession, envy, shame, and crooked gaze impute comic rasa to the false prattle of all people. The commentary makes all auspicious.

[gita-a09-v36] Here is the summary verse: in non-dual Brahman the supreme Power, full of grace to all, unfolds; therefore one should strive to attain it.
