[gita-a10-v01] The Lord says he will speak his supreme word again to Arjuna, who is pleased, out of desire for his welfare.

[gita-a10-v02] Neither gods nor great sages know his origin; he is indeed the beginning of gods and great sages in every way.

[gita-a10-v03] Whoever knows me as unborn, beginningless, and great lord of the world, being undeluded, is freed from all sins among mortals.

[gita-a10-v04] Intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion, forgiveness, truth, self-control, calm, pleasure, pain, becoming, being, fear, fearlessness, non-delusion, and zeal are listed.

[gita-a10-v05] Non-harm, equanimity, contentment, austerity, giving, fame, and infamy become various states of beings from me alone.

[gita-a10-v06] The seven former great sages and four Manus are born from my mind-born nature, and these creatures of the world are theirs.

[gita-a10-v07] Whoever truly knows this glory and yoga is united by unshaken yoga; there is no doubt here.

[gita-a10-v08] I am the source of all; all proceeds from me; thus the wise, endowed with devotion, worship me.

[gita-a10-v09] With minds fixed on me and lives gone to me, they enlighten and tell of me always, delighting one another through mutual knowing; all knowers are one Lord, attained easily by pervasion.

[gita-a10-v10] To those constantly united and worshipping with love, I give that wisdom-yoga by which they reach me.

[gita-a10-v11] For their compassion, I, abiding in self-state, destroy ignorance-born darkness with the shining lamp of knowledge.

[gita-a10-v12] Arjuna said: you are supreme Brahman, supreme abode, pure, highest person, eternal, divine first god, unborn, all-pervading.

[gita-a10-v13] The sages all say this of you, and likewise the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala, and Vyasa; you yourself also speak to me.

[gita-a10-v14] I think all this is true, O Kesava, that you speak to me; for neither gods nor great sages know your manifestation, O Lord.

[gita-a10-v15] You yourself know yourself by yourself, O best of persons, creator of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.

[gita-a10-v16] You should tell completely the auspicious glories of yourself, by which glories you pervade and stand in all these worlds.

[gita-a10-v17] How may I know you, O yogi, while I consider you? In which and which states are you to be thought, O Lord, by me?

[gita-a10-v18] Tell again in detail your yoga and glory, O Janardana; for there is no satisfaction for me hearing this nectar.

[gita-a10-v19] The blessed Lord said: indeed, I will tell you my auspicious glories chiefly, best of Kurus; there is no end to my expansion.

[gita-a10-v20] I am the self, Guḍākeśa, dwelling in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, middle, and indeed the end of beings.

[gita-a10-v21] Among Ādityas I am Viṣṇu, among lights the sun with rays; among Maruts I am Marīci, and among stars I am the moon.

[gita-a10-v22] Among Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; among gods I am Vāsava; among senses I am mind; among beings I am consciousness.

[gita-a10-v23] Among Rudras I am Śaṅkara; among Yakṣas and Rākṣasas I am the lord of wealth; among Vasus I am fire; among peaks I am Meru.

[gita-a10-v24] And know, Pārtha, Bṛhaspati as chief among priests; among army leaders I am Skanda; among rivers I am the ocean.

[gita-a10-v25] Among great sages I am Bhṛgu; among speeches the one imperishable syllable; among sacrifices the sacrifice of muttered prayer; among immovable things Himalaya.

[gita-a10-v26] Among all trees the sacred fig tree; among divine sages Nārada; among gandharvas Citraratha; among perfected ones Kapila the sage.

[gita-a10-v27] Know me as the swift one among horses, Airāvata among lordly elephants, and the lord of men among men.

[gita-a10-v28] I am the thunderbolt among weapons, the wish-cow among cows, Kandarpa as procreation, and Vāsuki among serpents.

[gita-a10-v29] I am Ananta among serpents, Varuṇa among aquatic beings, Aryaman among ancestors, and Yama among controllers.

[gita-a10-v30] I am Prahlāda among daityas, time among those who reckon, the lion king among beasts, and Vainateya among birds.

[gita-a10-v31] I am the wind among purifiers, Rama among weapon-bearers, the makara among fishes, and the Ganga among rivers.

[gita-a10-v32] Of creations I am the beginning, the end, and the middle too, O Arjuna; of knowledges, self-knowledge; of debates, I am the speech among speakers.

[gita-a10-v33] Of letters I am the a-sound, and the dual among compounds; I am imperishable time, and I the ordainer facing all directions.

[gita-a10-v34] Death is all-seizing and the origin of I among future things; fame, prosperity, and speech belong to women; memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and forgiveness are also named.

[gita-a10-v35] Among the samans I am the Brihat-saman; among meters I am Gayatri; among months I am Margashirsha; among seasons I am the flower-maker.

[gita-a10-v36] I am gambling among the fraudulent, splendor among the splendid, victory, resolve, and goodness among the good.

[gita-a10-v37] Among the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; among the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya; among sages, Vyāsa; among poets, Uśanas the poet.

[gita-a10-v38] I am the rod among punishers, policy among conquerors; and indeed I am silence among secrets, knowledge among knowers.

[gita-a10-v39] Whatever is the seed of all beings, that I am, Arjuna; nothing exists without me, no being moving or still.

[gita-a10-v40] There is no end, Parantapa, to my divine glories; this extent of glory has been spoken by me briefly.

[gita-a10-v41] Whatever being is glorious, splendid, or mighty, know that very thing, you, to be born of a spark of my splendor.

[gita-a10-v42] Or else, what is the use of much knowledge for you, Arjuna? Supporting this whole world, I stand with one part. I am the Self. This teaching prevents a distinction that would otherwise break the vision of Brahman; all this is the Lord's principle, manifested in various forms and becoming the object of all.

[gita-a10-v43] Here is the summary verse: whatever comes within desire or sense, forcibly dissolve it and meditate peaceful brahman. Thus in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, tenth chapter.

[gita-a11-v01] Now the eleventh chapter: Arjuna asks to make directly seen the very meaning stated in the preceding chapter, since what is understood through teaching becomes clear when mounted by direct cognition; therefore these statements and replies are spoken. Arjuna said: for my grace you spoke the supreme secret called self-knowledge; by that speech this delusion of mine is gone.

[gita-a11-v02] Birth and dissolution of beings have indeed been heard by me in detail from you, lotus-petal-eyed one; your greatness and imperishability too.

[gita-a11-v03] Thus this is as you said: I wish to see you yourself, supreme lord, your divine form, O best of persons.

[gita-a11-v04] If you think that is possible for me to see, O lord, lord of yogis, then show me your imperishable self.

[gita-a11-v05] The blessed Lord said: see, O son of Pritha, my forms by hundreds and by thousands, of various kinds, divine, of various colors and forms.

[gita-a11-v06] See the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, and Maruts, and many things never seen before; see wonders, O son of Pandu.

[gita-a11-v07] Here, in one place, see the whole world, moving and still, in my body, Guḍākeśa, and whatever else you wish to see.

[gita-a11-v08] But you cannot see me with this own eye; I give you a divine eye: see my divine form.

[gita-a11-v09] Saṃjaya said: having said thus, then, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed to Pārtha the supreme divine form.

[gita-a11-v10] Many mouths and eyes, many wondrous sights; many divine ornaments; divine, many raised weapons.

[gita-a11-v11] Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrance, full of all wonders, divine and endless, with faces everywhere.

[gita-a11-v12] If the splendor of a thousand suns were to rise at once in heaven, that might be like the splendor of that great soul.

[gita-a11-v13] Then Arjuna saw the whole world, divided in many ways, in one place in the body of the god of gods.

[gita-a11-v14] Then Arjuna, filled with wonder, hair standing on end, bowed with his head and spoke to the god with folded hands.

[gita-a11-v15] Arjuna said: I see your gods in your body, O god, and all groups of beings, Brahma the lord seated on the lotus, sages, and all divine serpents.

[gita-a11-v16] I see you with many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, endless in form on every side; I see no end, no middle, and no beginning again, O lord of the universe, universal form!

[gita-a11-v17] I see you crowned, mace-bearing, and discus-bearing, a mass of radiance on all sides, radiant; I see you hard to look at, all around, immeasurable in blazing fire, sun, and radiance.

[gita-a11-v18] You are the imperishable supreme to be known; you are the supreme treasury of this universe; you are imperishable, protector of sattvata dharma, eternal person, in my thought. Thus the principle known by those whose dharma is continuous grasping and renunciation, transcending all paths, is protected; this very secret in this chapter has mostly been revealed by me in the goddess-hymn commentary, and by those of like heart with instruction it is understood by itself. What again, by clearer manifestation and speech?

[gita-a11-v19] I see you, infinite in power and arms, moon-and-sun-eyed, with a blazing fire-mouth, scorching this universe by your own radiance.

[gita-a11-v20] Indeed, this interval between heaven and earth is pervaded by you alone, and all directions; seeing your wonderful fierce form, the three worlds are agitated, great soul.

[gita-a11-v21] Indeed these god-hosts enter into you; some frightened ones, with joined palms, praise, saying svasti; and great-sage hosts hymn you with abundant praises.

[gita-a11-v22] Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Viśve, Aśvins, Maruts, Uṣmapās, and Gandharva, Yakṣa, Asura, and Siddha hosts all behold you, astonished.

[gita-a11-v23] Seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs, feet, bellies, tusks, and fangs, the worlds are agitated, and so am I.

[gita-a11-v24] Seeing you, whose form touches the sky, blazing in many colors, with open mouth and blazing wide eyes, my inner self is agitated; I find neither steadiness nor peace, O Viṣṇu.

[gita-a11-v25] Seeing your fang-terrifying mouths, like death-fire, I know no directions and find no comfort; be gracious, lord of gods, abode of the world.

[gita-a11-v26] All these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with groups of earth-protectors, Bhishma, Drona, that charioteer's son, and our own warrior chiefs, are seen.

[gita-a11-v27] Hurrying, they enter your fang-terrifying fearful mouths; some are seen stuck between the teeth with crushed heads.

[gita-a11-v28] Men of various forms, being crushed, enter your mouth of inconceivable form; Yudhishthira's and Dhritarashtra's warriors, all cut by various weapons, enter indeed.

[gita-a11-v29] Surely these are slain by your radiance; for thus these have entered your body, as many river currents flow toward the ocean indeed.

[gita-a11-v30] Thus your world-heroes enter the blazing mouths around, as moths enter blazing fire for destruction with swift force; so too worlds enter your mouths for destruction with swift force.

[gita-a11-v31] You lick and devour all worlds on every side with blazing mouths; filling the whole world with radiance, your fierce rays scorch, O Viṣṇu.

[gita-a11-v32] Tell me who you are, fierce-formed one; homage to you, best of gods, be gracious. I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not know your course; I do not know why such a fierce form arises.

[gita-a11-v33] The blessed Lord said: I am Time, grown and world-destroying; I am engaged here to gather worlds. Even without you, all warriors stationed in opposing ranks will not be.

[gita-a11-v34] Therefore rise, gain glory; having conquered enemies, enjoy prosperous rule. These have already been slain by me; be a mere instrument, left-handed archer.

[gita-a11-v35] Slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and other world-heroes; they have been slain by me, so do not be distressed; fight, and you will conquer rivals in battle. This here is the Lord's reply concerning the world's knowing-and-unknowing self; it is said that from pure, impure, and mixed awareness there is devouring. You fed the secret summarized in this chapter; may it be for those capable of immediate awareness. How much labor of line-writing; may we rest in stability. Here what was said by me: when they are slain, you, glorious one, be instrument. Thus by the Lord that was replied to what was said earlier by Arjuna: we do not know this; which of us is greater, and so on.

[gita-a11-v36] Sañjaya said: having heard this speech of Keśava, the crowned one, with folded hands and trembling, bowed again and indeed said to Kṛṣṇa with faltering voice, greatly frightened, having prostrated.

[gita-a11-v37] Arjuna said: 'It is fitting, Hrishikesha, that by your praise the world rejoices and delights; frightened demons flee in all directions; and groups of siddhas bow.'

[gita-a11-v38] Why do these not bow to the greater first creator Brahman? Because you, endless lord of gods and abode of the world, are the imperishable beyond true and false; false appearance is not an object as true meaning; or even nonbeing, joined to its own distinctive word and attaining knowledge-form, is not other than supreme Brahman-being; and that form is perceived in the concealment of both true and false cognition.

[gita-a11-v39] You are the primordial god, the ancient person; you are the supreme treasure of this universe; you are the knower and the knowable, the supreme abode; by you the universe of infinite form is pervaded.

[gita-a11-v40] You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and great-grandfather; beginningless, measureless, unmatched being; lord of all; O all-great manifestation.

[gita-a11-v41] Arjuna repeatedly salutes the lord from every side; through praise the lord's own form becomes directly perceptible, so further commentary is stopped to avoid repetition.

[gita-a11-v42] No other is seen in the three worlds; the lord of inconceivable action, endless vigor, and unmeasured valor pervades all, therefore he is all.

[gita-a11-v43] Thinking you were my friend, I spoke forcibly, O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend; not knowing your greatness, I did this by carelessness or affection.

[gita-a11-v44] Whatever disrespect was shown to you for mockery, in play, bed, seat, or food, alone or before others, O Acyuta, I beg your pardon, immeasurable one.

[gita-a11-v45] You are father of the moving and still world, venerable teacher of this universe; none is equal to you, much less superior, in the three worlds of unmatched splendor.

[gita-a11-v46] Therefore bowing and placing my body, I propitiate you, worshipful Lord; as a father bears a son, as a friend bears a friend, O god, you should endure.

[gita-a11-v47] The sages remember your divine and wondrous former deeds; no other is doer of the world; you alone are sustainer, ordainer, and all-pervading Bhava.

[gita-a11-v48] What wondrous thing of yours would be unbearable, or what could be possible from another? I will proclaim, since you are doer of all, O vibhu; therefore all this is you alone.

[gita-a11-v49] Your action is extremely wondrous and not difficult; no comparison for your action is found; not even your qualities have measure, nor your splendor, strength, or glory.

[gita-a11-v50] Having seen this never-before-seen form, I am rejoiced and my mind is greatly distressed by fear; show me that very form, O god, be gracious, O lord of gods, abode of the world.

[gita-a11-v51] I desire to see you crowned, mace-bearing, discus in hand; just so, by that very four-armed form, O thousand-armed one, be, O world-form.

[gita-a11-v52] The blessed Lord said: by me, being gracious, this supreme form was shown to you, Arjuna, by self-yoga; radiant, world, infinite, primal, which by other than you has not been seen before.

[gita-a11-v53] Not by Veda, sacrifice, study, nor by gifts, nor by rites, nor by severe austerities can such a form be seen by me in the human world by other than you, O Kuru hero.

[gita-a11-v54] Let there be no distress for you, nor confusion, having seen this terrible fierce form of mine; with fear gone and pleased mind, again you behold that very gentle form of mine.

[gita-a11-v55] Sanjaya said that Vasudeva, having spoken thus to Arjuna, showed his own form again, consoled the frightened one, and became the great soul of gentle form.

[gita-a11-v56] Arjuna said that having seen this gentle human form of Krishna, he is now restored, of sound mind, and returned to his nature; at the end of total withdrawal the Lord gives the supremely peaceful form, the state of Brahman-principle, and thus in conclusion the Lord's gentleness.

[gita-a11-v57] The blessed Lord said: this form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods always desire to see this form.

[gita-a11-v58] I am not to be seen in such a form by the Vedas, nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice; you have seen me as I am.

[gita-a11-v59] By undivided devotion I can be known, seen, and entered in truth in such a form, O Arjuna, scorcher of foes.

[gita-a11-v60] He who does my works, is devoted to me, is free from attachment, and is without enmity toward all beings reaches me, O Pandava. For those whose devotion shines forth toward no other knowable pleasant thing, Vasudeva approaches them; all. From the wonder of the previously stated teaching, the world-souled Vasudeva-principle descends effortlessly into the path of knowing. Auspicious. 60.

[gita-a11-v61] Here is the summary verse: through recognition of the unity of consciousness arising from pure, impure, and mixed states, the sage who sees earth, midworld, and the three worlds with equality is equal.

[gita-a12-v01] Arjuna asks which devotees are most accomplished in yoga, those who worship the Lord or those who worship the unmanifest.

[gita-a12-v02] The Lord declares that devotees who enter him with mind and worship him with supreme faith are most united.

[gita-a12-v03] Those who worship the imperishable, indescribable, unmanifest, all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, and firm.

[gita-a12-v04] By restraining the senses and being equal-minded everywhere, devoted to all beings' welfare, they attain me alone.

[gita-a12-v05] The unmanifest path is hard for embodied beings; even Brahman-worshippers attain the Lord, but with greater effort.

[gita-a12-v06] Those who renounce all actions into me, devoted to me, meditate on me through yoga and worship.

[gita-a12-v07] For those whose minds are fixed in me, I, O Partha, become the deliverer from the ocean of death and samsara, and not after a long time.

[gita-a12-v08] Place your mind in me alone and fix your intellect in me; you will dwell in me, abiding in supreme yoga. Those who renounce everything in me through the previously stated teaching are rescued by me from all obstacles and afflictions. The entering of mind is explained. This yoga is supreme because it is unartificial. When knowledge is awakened through the manifestation of distinguished means, posture, abiding, and samadhi possibility in my hymn, that is not your ever-flowing innate consciousness; because of the triad's presence, consciousness is clearly perceived here too. But when fuel-less, taking self-mastery and indifference to the body, consciousness suddenly knows itself and the fire of knowledge arises at once. Then, goddess, free from the supports of that body-person, one knows the great lord, who agitates the bonds of the powerless, and so forth.

[gita-a12-v09] You cannot make the mind enter steadily into me by practice-yoga alone; then, O Dhanañjaya, to obtain me, without intense descent of divine power and long-pleased guru foot grace, absorption is difficult—thus practice.

[gita-a12-v10] Even if you cannot practice, be devoted to right action; by performing actions for my sake you will attain perfection. Since practice is hindered by obstacles, therefore perform actions, worship, recitation, study, sacrifice, and the like to destroy them.

[gita-a12-v11] Even if you are established in my yoga but unable to do this, renounce the fruits of all actions and remain self-controlled. If, from ignorance, you cannot perform divine action, then renounce all of it to me through self-offering, according to the method stated in scripture. Relying on that intent, I have spoken in an easy procedure. Whatever is deficient, excessive, unknown, lacking sequence, lacking attention, or a slip of intellect, forgive mercifully, O Shambhu, since you are full of compassion. By this yoga of hymn I offer your self; again, causelessly, I attain fitness for sufferings. In the supreme lordly doctrinal scriptures, this very intent is that of self-offering; this meaning is summarized.

[gita-a12-v12] Knowledge is better than practice; meditation surpasses knowledge; from meditation comes renunciation of fruits and then peace. Since knowledge is absorption and practice's fruit is absorption, meditation as divine fullness is distinguished and attains desired realization; then action-fruits can be renounced, otherwise renunciation is nowhere; ultimate peace follows renunciation. Therefore absorption-natured knowledge, root of all, is principal.

[gita-a12-v13] The devotee who does not hate any being, is friendly and compassionate, free of mine-ness and ego, equal in pain and joy, and forgiving is dear to the Lord.

[gita-a12-v14] The yogi who is always content, self-controlled, firmly resolved, and has offered mind and intellect to the Lord is dear to the Lord.

[gita-a12-v15] He who does not agitate the world, is not agitated by it, and is freed from joy, anger, fear, and agitation is dear to the Lord.

[gita-a12-v16] The devotee who expects nothing, is pure and skillful, remains indifferent, is free from pain, and renounces the fruits of all undertakings is dear to the Lord.

[gita-a12-v17] He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, and renounces the fruits of good and bad is dear to the Lord.

[gita-a12-v18] Equal toward enemy and friend, in honor and dishonor, in cold, heat, pleasure, and pain, and free from attachment.

[gita-a12-v19] One who is equal in blame and praise, silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded, and devoted is dear to me.

[gita-a12-v20] Those who faithfully practice this immortal dharma are exceedingly dear; one without fixed resolve, accepting what comes and absorbed in the supreme Lord, easily attains supreme isolation.

[gita-a12-v21] Here is the summary verse: the wealth of absorption born from supreme bliss is itself Brahman-being in all states, attained without effort.

[gita-a13-v01] Arjuna said: O Keśava, I wish to know nature and person, field and field-knower, knowledge and the knowable. Scripture somewhere says the field-knower is to be worshipped; is he the Self or the Lord, or some third other? Thus, amid this question and doubt, the holy Lord instructs.

[gita-a13-v02] The blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field; he who knows this, the knowers of that call the field-knower.

[gita-a13-v03] Know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata; the knowing of field and knower of the field — that is deemed knowing by Me. The body of transmigrators is the field, wherein karma-seeds sprout; hence their self, stained by adventitious impurity, is called the knower; for the awakened it is the same field distinctly.

[gita-a13-v04] Hear from me in brief what that field is, of what kind, with what modifications, from what, what it is, who its knower is, and of what nature.

[gita-a13-v05] Although sages and Vedas have taught this in many ways, through various meters and reasoned Brahmasūtra words, distinguishing transformation and the transformed by a common answer without distinction, I will explain it in summary.

[gita-a13-v06] The great elements, ego, intellect, and unmanifest; the senses are eleven, and five are sense-objects; the unmanifest is nature; senses with mind are eleven; sense-objects are forms and the rest, five.

[gita-a13-v07] Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, aggregate consciousness, and steadiness are this field in brief; consciousness-seeing power is the person. Thus the field is explained, and the field-knower; now knowledge is declared.

[gita-a13-v08] Humility, nonpretense, nonviolence, patience, straightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-restraint.

[gita-a13-v09] Dispassion and non-egoism in sense objects, and seeing the faults of birth, death, age, disease, and suffering.

[gita-a13-v10] Non-attachment and non-clinging in son, wife, house, and so on, and always equal-mindedness in desired and undesired occurrences.

[gita-a13-v11] Unwavering devotion to me by non-other yoga, residence in a secluded place, and dislike for crowds.

[gita-a13-v12] Steadfastness in self-knowledge and seeing the purpose of truth-knowledge are this knowledge; what is otherwise is ignorance. Certainty that nothing apart from the supreme self exists is yoga; by that certainty devotion to me does not deviate. Thus everything is to be connected; the opposite of this is ignorance, and pride and the rest. By this knowledge what is to be known is declared.

[gita-a13-v13] I shall declare that which is to be known, by knowing which one eats immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, called neither existent nor nonexistent.

[gita-a13-v14] Everywhere are its hands and feet; everywhere its eyes, heads, and mouths; everywhere hearing in the world; having pervaded all, it stands.

[gita-a13-v15] It is the reflection of all sense qualities, yet devoid of all senses; unattached, bearer of all, without strands, and enjoyer of strands.

[gita-a13-v16] It is outside and inside beings, moving and unmoving; because of subtlety it is unknowable, far and near.

[gita-a13-v17] Undivided in beings, yet as if divided, it stands; bearer of beings, that to-be-known, devouring and ruling.

[gita-a13-v18] That light beyond darkness is called supreme; knowing and known, reachable by knowing, it abides in the heart of all; beginningless supreme Brahman, by qualifiers beginning with Brahman indicating and supporting Brahman's nature, non-different from knowledge stated by all doctrines, is declared. These qualifiers were already explained; what fruitless repetition?

[gita-a13-v19] This field, knowing, and the known are stated in brief; one who knows this triad is the Lord's devotee and attains the Lord's state.

[gita-a13-v20] Know nature and person as beginningless, along with modifications and strands born from nature.

[gita-a13-v21] Nature is called the cause in action and instrumentality, while person is called the cause in enjoying pleasures and pains.

[gita-a13-v22] The person standing in nature enjoys strands born from nature; attachment to strands causes births, and nature and person function in mutual dependence.

[gita-a13-v23] The supreme person in the body is witness, consenter, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord; nature, its fourteen-fold modification, and creation are beginningless and eternal.

[gita-a13-v24] One who knows person, nature, strands, and modifications is not born again; even while acting, such a yogi is liberated.

[gita-a13-v25] Some see the self by meditation, others by sāṃkhya, yoga, or karma-yoga.

[gita-a13-v26] Others, not knowing thus, hear from others and worship; they too cross death.

[gita-a13-v27] Whatever exists, moving or still, arises from field-knower union; nothing exists beyond the knower.

[gita-a13-v28] He who sees the supreme lord standing equally in all beings, perishing with the perishing, truly sees.

[gita-a13-v29] Seeing the lord equally everywhere, one does not harm oneself and reaches the supreme goal.

[gita-a13-v30] Seeing actions done by nature and the self as non-doer, one truly sees.

[gita-a13-v31] When one sees distinct beings as unified, then brahman is attained.

[gita-a13-v32] The beginningless, qualityless supreme self, though in the body, neither acts nor is stained.

[gita-a13-v33] As space remains unstained, so the self remains unstained even in the body.

[gita-a13-v34] As the sun illuminates the world, the supreme self illuminates all fields.

[gita-a13-v35] Those who know the difference between field and knower attain supreme Shiva.

[gita-a13-v36] Here is the summary verse: confused minds see person and nature as distinct, while the complete see the world as pure self.

[gita-a14-v01] Now the fourteenth chapter. The blessed Lord said: I will again declare the supreme, highest knowledge among knowledges, by knowing which all sages attained supreme siddhi. That very knowledge previously stated I will again speak with excellence, individually determining the nature of the gunas, in full detail. By 'having known which,' he declares the evident certainty and establishment of this knowledge.

[gita-a14-v02] Having relied on this knowledge and attained sameness with me, they are not born even in creation, nor are they distressed in dissolution.

[gita-a14-v03] My womb is the great Brahman; in it I place the seed; thence comes the birth of all beings, O Bhārata. For what is to be abandoned, once its cause is known, is easy — I, of unspeakable bliss-form, taking up my own expanding power as Brahman, my reflective power over beginningless atoms, set them transmigrating for grace.

[gita-a14-v04] O son of Kunti, all forms arise in every womb; of them Brahman is the great womb, and I am the seed-giver and father. In all wombs, as primordial cause, the nourishing divine power whose nature is the vomiting-forth of all samsara is mother, and I am called father, possessor of power.

[gita-a14-v05] The qualities sattva, rajas, and tamas, born of nature, bind the imperishable embodied self in the body; and this embodied one, identifying those guna-dharmas as self, is bound by them for enjoyment up to liberation.

[gita-a14-v06] There, sattva, being pure, illuminating, and free from disease, binds by attachment to pleasure and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.

[gita-a14-v07] Know rajas to be passion-natured, born of craving and attachment; that, O Kaunteya, binds the embodied one through attachment to action. In order, their form is said to be pure sattva, because craving is the origin of attachment.

[gita-a14-v08] Know that tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all embodied beings and binds them through negligence, laziness, and sleep. O Bharata, even rare human birth, gained by long-accumulated merit and the one cause of liberation, is wasted by negligence. Thus it is said: one moment of life cannot be obtained with all jewels; he who leads it vainly is negligent and the lowest man. Laziness in auspicious deeds is complete sleep, and sleep is a despised state.

[gita-a14-v09] O Bharata, sattva binds in happiness, rajas in action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds in delusion.

[gita-a14-v10] O Bharata, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva becomes dominant; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. Thus, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva increases; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. It is said that the increase of a guṇa comes by mutual overcoming.

[gita-a14-v11] When knowledge arises as light in all the gates of this body, then know that sattva has increased.

[gita-a14-v12] Greed, activity, restlessness in action, and thirst arise and grow when rajas predominates, O best of the Bharatas.

[gita-a14-v13] When tamas increases, darkness, inertia, delusion, and confusion arise; when rajas increases, greed and related qualities arise gradually through all the senses.

[gita-a14-v14] When sattva increases, the embodied one goes to dissolution and attains pure worlds; through unbroken sattvic practice, increased sattva brings auspicious attainment.

[gita-a14-v15] Dissolution in rajas leads birth among action-bound beings; dissolution in tamas leads birth in deluded wombs; habitual tamas leads hell, animal, or tree births.

[gita-a14-v16] Good action yields pure sattvic fruit; rajas yields suffering and ignorance; tamas yields its own fruit.

[gita-a14-v17] From sattva arises knowledge; from rajas arises greed, delusion, and confusion; from tamas arises ignorance.

[gita-a14-v18] Those established in sattva go upward; rajas ones remain in the middle; tamas ones go downward.

[gita-a14-v19] When the seer sees no agent other than the strands and knows what is beyond them, he attains my nature.

[gita-a14-v20] Having transcended these three strands, the embodied one, freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, tastes immortality.

[gita-a14-v21] Arjuna asks by what signs, conduct, and means one transcends these three strands.

[gita-a14-v22] The Lord says one who neither hates illumination, activity, and delusion nor desires their arising or cessation becomes strand-transcending.

[gita-a14-v23] Seated like an indifferent one, not shaken by the strands, knowing they operate, the unwise stands and does not move.

[gita-a14-v24] Equal in pain and pleasure, in clod, stone, and gold, in pleasant and unpleasant, the steady one is equal in blame and self-praise.

[gita-a14-v25] He who is equal in honor and dishonor, friend and foe, abandoning fruits of all undertakings, is called beyond the strands; though appearing ignorant, he stands without discrimination, and from right knowing he does not fall from his own form.

[gita-a14-v26] Who serves me with unwavering devotion-yoga transcends these strands and becomes fit for brahman-becoming; this is the root means taught, and the one who serves me alone without desiring fruit is purified by the Lord's foremost power.

[gita-a14-v27] I am the foundation of brahman, the immortal and imperishable, and of eternal duty and absolute happiness; when I am served, brahman becomes, otherwise worshipped brahman remains inert and would give liberation no different from deep sleep.

[gita-a14-v28] Here is the summary verse: shining with devotion-rasa absorption and free from ego-delusion, even when strands conflict, the guṇa-transcendent ascetic remains equal.

[gita-a15-v01] Now the fifteenth chapter: the Lord said the imperishable asvattha has its root above and branches below; its leaves are the vedic meters, and whoever knows it is a knower of the veda.

[gita-a15-v02] Its branches spread up and down, grown by the strands and bearing sense-objects as shoots; below, roots extend, bound to action, in the human world.

[gita-a15-v03] Its form is not perceived here thus; it has no end, no beginning, no stable foundation; this deeply rooted asvattha must be cut with the sharpened weapon of non-attachment.

[gita-a15-v04] Then that state is to be sought, to which having gone one does not return again; I take refuge in that very first person, from whom the ancient emanation has spread.

[gita-a15-v05] The unconfused, free from pride and delusion, go to the imperishable state; its actions, rooted below, are to be cut, and that tranquil imperishable state alone is the goal.

[gita-a15-v06] Neither sun nor moon nor fire illumines it; having gone there one does not return; that supreme abode of mine is beyond the limitation of space, time, and instruments.

[gita-a15-v07] The eternal living being draws mind and senses in the living world; its portionhood of Brahman is figurative, not a real division.

[gita-a15-v08] The lord obtains and leaves bodies, carrying the subtle instruments with him, as wind carries scent from place to place.

[gita-a15-v09] Presiding over ear, eye, touch, taste, smell, and mind, this self enjoys the objects.

[gita-a15-v10] The deluded do not see the self standing, departing, or enjoying; the awakened see its knowing form everywhere.

[gita-a15-v11] Striving yogis see the self established in the self, but unperfected selves do not; effort alone does not yield fullness.

[gita-a15-v12] Know the light residing in sun, moon, and fire, which illuminates the whole world, to be mine.

[gita-a15-v13] Entering the earth, I sustain beings by my energy and nourish all herbs, having become the moon, the essence of sap.

[gita-a15-v14] I become the universal fire, abiding in the bodies of living beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, and cook the fourfold food. The venerable teachers say that the world-sustaining power of the five elements, as whole and part, is the Lord's māheśvarya. The sun's light illuminates and sustains; the moon's light illuminates and nourishes herbs; fire's light illuminates, dries, burns, sweats, and cooks; and space is all-pervading as awareness-space. Therefore, having stated the knowable form, he shows the self as supreme Lord, all-knowing, independent, and all-maker.

[gita-a15-v15] I dwell in the heart of all; from me come memory, knowledge, and removal. I alone am known by all the Vedas and Vedanta. The knowable nature is independent knowing, and the reflection 'there I am' is knowledge as new manifestation and world-creation. Conceptual knowledge is removal, bond-creation, and maya-made fixation; remembering is the residue of withdrawn impressions manifesting again. Thus all knowledges are withdrawn, and agency as freedom preceded by omniscience is declared. All scriptures determine the supreme Lord-principle alone; the Lord's freedom is world-agency through creating, uprooting, and re-establishing own nature. Others, by difference-cognition, make removal and thereby produce Vedanta and Veda through self-realization.

[gita-a15-v16] In the world there are two persons: the perishable and the imperishable. The perishable is all beings, while the immutable is called imperishable.

[gita-a15-v17] Another highest person, called the supreme self, enters the three worlds and sustains the imperishable Lord.

[gita-a15-v18] Because I transcend both the perishable and the imperishable, I am supreme; therefore I am renowned in the world and in the Veda as the supreme person. The text says there are these two persons in the world. Even in an unawakened state, people know the conscious self with a body made of elements as perishable form, and from the world's delusion the dualistic view does not cease. But I, all-gracious, split the dualistic knot and, pervading all the world, am to be known. I transcend the perishable because beings are inert, and the imperishable because all-pervasion is denied in the unawakened self. Thus, by explanations beginning with the supreme person in world and Veda, he alone is said to be the supreme nondual self.

[gita-a15-v19] One who knows the supreme person without delusion worships with all being; all forms, actions, and knowledge are recognized as the Lord.

[gita-a15-v20] This most secret scripture is completed by understanding nondual recognition; accomplishment comes from knowing, not from action, and the goal is absorption in the Lord.

[gita-a15-v21] Having removed great duality-delusion and made consciousness Brahman-filled, the sage always enters it even in worldly practice.

[gita-a16-v01] Now the sixteenth chapter: after scripture-based knowing, reasoned meditation arises; the Lord lists divine qualities beginning with fearlessness.

[gita-a16-v02] Non-harm, truth, non-anger, renunciation, non-attachment, non-slander, compassion, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and non-restlessness.

[gita-a16-v03] Energy, patience, steadfastness, contentment, non-malice, and absence of excessive pride are the divine wealth of one born divine, Bharata.

[gita-a16-v04] Hypocrisy, pride, egoism, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the demonic wealth, Partha.

[gita-a16-v05] Divine wealth liberates, demonic wealth binds; Arjuna is born divine, so he should not grieve.

[gita-a16-v06] In this world there are two creature-creations, divine and demonic; the divine was spoken in detail, now hear the demonic, Partha.

[gita-a16-v07] This divine wealth is described by abhaya and so on; demonic people do not know activity or cessation, and purity, conduct, and truth are not found in them.

[gita-a16-v08] They call the world untrue, unstable, lordless, and causeless; they see no effect beyond what is seen.

[gita-a16-v09] Relying on this view, lost selves with small intellects arise as fierce actors, inauspicious for the world's destruction.

[gita-a16-v10] Relying on insatiable desire, filled with pride, conceit, and intoxication, they act cruelly with impure vows.

[gita-a16-v11] Relying on immeasurable anxiety until dissolution, making desire-enjoyment supreme, they are certain only this much exists.

[gita-a16-v12] Bound by hundreds of hope-nooses and devoted to desire and anger, they strive unjustly to gather wealth for desire-enjoyment; their anxiety continues until transmigration and dissolution cease.

[gita-a16-v13] Today I have gained this; I shall obtain this desire; this is mine and this too; wealth will be mine again.

[gita-a16-v14] That enemy was slain by me; I will slay others too; I am lord, enjoyer, accomplished, strong, and happy.

[gita-a16-v15] I am wealthy and of noble birth; who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, give, and rejoice; thus they are deluded by ignorance.

[gita-a16-v16] Many-minded and confused, gone under delusion's control, attached to sense enjoyments, they fall into impure hell; lacking certainty, they fall into hell beginning with avīci, in the continuum of birth and death.

[gita-a16-v17] Self-conceited, stiff, filled with wealth, pride, and intoxication, they sacrifice by name, with hypocrisy and without rule.

[gita-a16-v18] Resorting to egoism, strength, pride, desire, and anger, hating the Lord in self and other bodies, they sacrifice by name; such sacrifices do not fruit, and hating worlds they hate the Lord, who is Vasudeva, the all-dwelling.

[gita-a16-v19] I continually cast those hateful cruel lowest men into asuri wombs.

[gita-a16-v20] Born in asuri wombs, deluded ones fail to reach me and go to the lowest state; hating ones act harmfully and cause hell-fall, so I cast them into asuri wombs.

[gita-a16-v21] Desire, anger, and greed are the threefold gate of hell and destruction of self; therefore one should abandon this triad.

[gita-a16-v22] Freed from these three dark gates, O Kaunteya, a man practices for self and then goes to the supreme destination.

[gita-a16-v23] This is not a human saying to disregard; scripture here is beginningless authority. One who abandons scriptural rule and acts from desire attains neither perfection, happiness, nor supreme destination.

[gita-a16-v24] Therefore scripture is authority for you in determining action and inaction; having known this, you should do scripturally prescribed action here. Abandoning scriptural rule and deliberating by one's own opinion leads to fall into hell, so do not determine action and inaction by self-intellect; this is the purport.

[gita-a16-v25] In ignorance, one should not determine duty by one's own intellect; rather, by the rule declared in scripture, and scripture itself increases knowing. Thus ends the sixteenth chapter of Abhinavagupta's Gathering of the Gita's Meaning.

[gita-a17-v01] Arjuna asks Krsna about the steadfastness of those who, endowed with faith, act beyond scriptural rule, and whether their nature is sattva, rajas, or tamas; the Lord's answer follows according to faith.

[gita-a17-v02] The Lord says faith is threefold by nature, then explains scripture as unbiased, firm reflection rooted in knowing-freedom, fruitful for sattva-possessors with controlled conduct.

[gita-a17-v03] Faith is according to one's sattva; a person is made of faith, and he becomes according to his faith.

[gita-a17-v04] Sattvic people worship gods, yakshas, and rakshasas; rajasic and tamasic people worship spirits, ghosts, and demons.

[gita-a17-v05] People joined with hypocrisy and ego, endowed with desire, attachment, and force, perform terrible austerity not prescribed by scripture.

[gita-a17-v06] Those who torment the body and the Lord within are demonic; they are connected to faith turned elsewhere, fashion self-made austerity, and are tamasic.

[gita-a17-v07] Food is threefold for all, and sacrifice, austerity, and gift are likewise threefold; hear this distinction.

[gita-a17-v08] Foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and affection, being tasty, unctuous, steady, and heart-pleasing, are dear to sattva.

[gita-a17-v09] Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry, and burning are desired by rajas and give pain, grief, and disease.

[gita-a17-v10] Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover, and impure is dear to tamas.

[gita-a17-v11] A sacrifice performed by those not desiring fruit, according to rule, with the mind fixed on duty alone, is sattvic.

[gita-a17-v12] Know that a sacrifice performed aiming at fruit and for show is rajasic, unsteady, and impermanent.

[gita-a17-v13] They declare tamasic a sacrifice that lacks rule, has unoffered food, lacks mantra, is giftless, and is devoid of faith. 'Lacking rule' means lacking scripture-prescribed action, and that same sacrifice is elaborated by qualifiers such as unoffered food.

[gita-a17-v14] Worship of gods, twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity and straightforwardness; celibacy and non-injury—this is called bodily austerity. Straightforwardness or rectitude, not concealing objects, and boldness are also mentioned.

[gita-a17-v15] Speech that does not distress, is true, pleasant, and beneficial is called speech-born austerity, along with self-study and practice. "Truth" means determining this very essential nature; "pleasant and beneficial" means pleasant at that time and beneficial at another time. Such speech is called truth, not merely recounting events.

[gita-a17-v16] Mental austerity is said to be mental serenity, gentleness, silence, self-control, and purity of being; purity of being is the complete purification of one's intention or inner disposition.

[gita-a17-v17] Men declare as sattvic the threefold austerity that is endowed with supreme faith and performed by those who are free from desire for fruit.

[gita-a17-v18] Austerity performed with hypocrisy for the sake of honor, respect, or worship is here declared rajasic, unstable, and impermanent.

[gita-a17-v19] Austerity performed with foolish self-torment or to destroy another is tamasic; in all three kinds, faith is sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic according to its aim.

[gita-a17-v20] A gift given to an unhelpful person at the right place and time to a worthy recipient is sattvic; mere obligation is only to be observed.

[gita-a17-v21] A gift given for reciprocal benefit or with an eye to fruit, or given in distress, is called rajasic.

[gita-a17-v22] A gift given at the wrong place or time to unworthy recipients, disrespectfully, is tamasic; worldly actions are explained by threefold intent, and now the manner of those beyond the three strands is stated.

[gita-a17-v23] Om tat sat is the threefold designation of brahman; by it brahmins, vedas, and sacrifices were prescribed formerly.

[gita-a17-v24] Therefore, uttering om, the prescribed actions of sacrifice, gift, and austerity proceed always among speakers of brahman.

[gita-a17-v25] Liberation-seekers perform various sacrifice, austerity, and gift actions without desiring their fruit.

[gita-a17-v26] The word sat is used in existence and goodness, and likewise in praiseworthy action; so, O Partha, sat is sung.

[gita-a17-v27] Steadiness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is called sat, and action done for that purpose is also called sat. Om, tat, and sat are three words that designate and manifest Brahman: om indicates scriptural meaning tied to embodiment, tat denotes generality and non-attachment to fruits, and sat declares praise. Action performed with a corrupt intellect becomes tamasic, while action done without attachment to specific fruits is not binding. Thus faithful sacrifice, austerity, and gift do not bind, whereas faithless action is tamasic and fruitless.

[gita-a17-v28] Whatever is offered, given, or done as austerity without faith is called asat; it avails neither here nor hereafter. Therefore those who strive in auspicious action attain śivam with ease.

[gita-a17-v29] Here is the summary verse: that is indeed agent-entry; action is non-distinct from it; nevertheless, for knowers, it culminates in liberation.

[gita-a18-v01] Arjuna said: O mighty-armed one, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Kesi-slayer, I desire to know separately the truth of renunciation and of abandonment. You previously said that the renouncer is wise, and that the ascetic and yogi are not fireless, and so on. Thus, hearing of these two renouncers, this question arises for one who wishes to know their distinction; here is the answer.

[gita-a18-v02] The blessed Lord said: the wise know renunciation of desired actions as complete renunciation; the discerning call renunciation of all action-fruits renunciation. Desired rites such as agniṣṭoma are all actions; for all nitya and naimittika actions, even while being performed, renunciation of the fruit is renunciation. What remains to be spoken in this chapter was expanded and examined by ancients such as Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara; for those whose essence is fulfilling the promise of merely clarifying hidden meaning, what is the effort of showing repetition? Here, for determining the distinction, opinions are presented.

[gita-a18-v03] Some say all action is defective and should be abandoned; others say sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not. Some distinguish by good fruit; others, like Sāṃkhya/Grhya followers, reject action tainted by violence and sin. Mīmāṃsakas hold sacrifice has a purpose known from scripture. Thus Vedic violence is not mere violence, and general prohibitions are overridden in that context; hawk-sacrifice violence pertains to fruit and meditative cognition. The learned therefore do not abandon sacrifices and similar rites even when joined with violence, since scripture alone distinguishes duty from non-duty.

[gita-a18-v04] Hear my determination about renunciation, best of the Bharatas; renunciation is indeed declared threefold, O tiger among men.

[gita-a18-v05] Sacrifice, gift, austerity, and action should not be abandoned; they must indeed be done. Sacrifice, gift, and austerity are purifiers for the wise.

[gita-a18-v06] Even these actions should be performed, abandoning attachment and their fruits; this is my certain supreme opinion, O Pārtha.

[gita-a18-v07] Renunciation of fixed action is unfit; abandonment from delusion is declared dark.

[gita-a18-v08] Who abandons action as pain from fear of bodily distress performs rajas abandonment and obtains no fruit of abandonment.

[gita-a18-v09] Fixed duty done while abandoning attachment and fruit is considered sattva abandonment.

[gita-a18-v10] A renouncer filled with sattva, wise and doubt-cut, neither hates unskillful action nor attaches to skillful action.

[gita-a18-v11] Since embodied beings cannot abandon all actions, one who abandons action-fruit is called a renouncer; true abandonment performs actions equally without attachment, aversion, or fruit-desire.

[gita-a18-v12] Threefold fruit of action comes to non-renouncers after death, never to renouncers; ignorant men, though causes stand, impose the whole burden of agency on the self and bind themselves by their own intellect, not by thing-state.

[gita-a18-v13] O mighty-armed, know from me these five causes spoken in settled doctrine for the success of all actions.

[gita-a18-v14] Basis, agent, instrument, various separate efforts, and divine are the five factors here.

[gita-a18-v15] Whatever action one begins by body, speech, or mind, right or opposite, these five are its causes.

[gita-a18-v16] Thus being so, one who sees only himself as agent, not seeing the five factors, is evil-minded.

[gita-a18-v17] One whose state is not ego-made and whose intellect is unstained is not bound even by killing.

[gita-a18-v18] Knowledge, knowable, and knower form a threefold impulsion of action; instrument, action, and agent form its gathering.

[gita-a18-v19] Knowledge, action, and agent are each declared threefold by strand-difference; hear them properly as the text enumerates their forms.

[gita-a18-v20] Know that knowledge as sattvic which sees one imperishable being, undivided, among divided beings such as gods and men.

[gita-a18-v21] But knowledge that knows many various beings as separate in all beings is remembered as rajasic, through an intellect of my pleasure and my hatred.

[gita-a18-v22] But knowledge attached to one task as a whole, causeless and small in true meaning, is called tamasic, arising from obsession and grasping anger and attachment.

[gita-a18-v23] Action that is fixed, done without attachment and aversion, by one not desiring fruit, is called sattvic.

[gita-a18-v24] But action done by one seeking desire, with ego, again and again, abundant in suffering and pervaded by ignorance and the rest, is remembered as rajasic.

[gita-a18-v25] Action begun from delusion, without considering consequence, destruction, violence, or manly effort, is called tamasic.

[gita-a18-v26] The agent free from attachment, endowed with steadfastness and zeal, unchanged in success or failure, is called sattvic; he does not say 'I am the doer,' yet even a yogi's conventional speech 'I do' is not forbidden.

[gita-a18-v27] The attached agent who desires fruit, is greedy, violent, impure, and joined with joy and sorrow in success and failure, is called rajasic.

[gita-a18-v28] The undisciplined, ordinary, stiff, deceitful, cruel, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating agent is called tamasic.

[gita-a18-v29] Hear completely and separately, Arjuna, the threefold distinction of intellect and steadfastness by the strands: intellect is decision, steadfastness is contentment; whatever good or bad is done is necessarily done, and steadfastness exists in all.

[gita-a18-v30] The intellect that knows activity and withdrawal, duty and non-duty, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, is considered sattvic, Arjuna.

[gita-a18-v31] The intellect by which one improperly knows right and wrong, duty and non-duty, is rajasic, O Pārtha.

[gita-a18-v32] The intellect joined with darkness, which understands wrong as right and reverses all meanings, is considered tamasic.

[gita-a18-v33] Steadfastness by which, through unwavering yoga, one holds mind, breath, and sense actions, is sattvic; thinking 'may I become self-delighting in every way,' one restrains them by yoga.

[gita-a18-v34] But steadfastness by which one holds duty, desire, and wealth, O Arjuna, with attachment and fruit-desire, is rajasic, O Pārtha; not by mere attachment but by such fixation.

[gita-a18-v35] Steadfastness by which the dull-minded one does not release sleep, fear, grief, despair, and delusion is tamasic; by which one binds contentment to those states, that too is tamasic steadfastness.

[gita-a18-v36] But now hear from me, O bull of the Bharatas, the threefold happiness, where one delights through practice and reaches the end of suffering.

[gita-a18-v37] That happiness which is sattvic is at first like poison but in the end like nectar; it is born from the clarity of self and mind, and at first practice it is hard to remove like poison because of long habituated attachment to objects, as scripture says the razor's edge is difficult to cross; mind-clarity arises from self-clarity because no other is needed.

[gita-a18-v38] That happiness which is from contact of objects and senses is at first like nectar but in the end like poison; it is called rajasic, born from mutual contact of objects and senses, like the eye's connection with form.

[gita-a18-v39] That happiness which at first and in continuation deludes the self, arising from sleep, laziness, and carelessness, is called tamasic; from sleep, by laziness and carelessness, as explained before, that happiness is tamasic.

[gita-a18-v40] No being on earth, in heaven, or among gods is free from the three strands; action, knowledge, and happiness are analyzed through their mutual relations, and the one abiding in sattvic wealth is fit for knowledge.

[gita-a18-v41] When concealment disappears, nature manifests; caste natures necessarily act, and actions are divided by nature-born strands.

[gita-a18-v42] Calmness, self-control, purity, patience, straightness, knowledge, discernment, and theism are brahmin nature-born action.

[gita-a18-v43] Heroism, splendor, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity, and lordliness are kshatriya action born of nature.

[gita-a18-v44] Farming, cattle protection, and trade are vaishya duty; service-based action is shudra duty, both born of nature.

[gita-a18-v45] A person engaged in his own duty obtains perfection; devoted to his own work he finds success; hear that.

[gita-a18-v46] From whom beings originate and by whom all this is pervaded, a human worshipping him through his own action finds success.

[gita-a18-v47] One's own duty, though deficient, is better than another's duty well performed; doing nature-fixed action one does not incur sin.

[gita-a18-v48] Kaunteya, one should not abandon innate action even if faulty, for all beginnings are covered by fault like fire by smoke.

[gita-a18-v49] One with unattached mind, self-conquered and free from desire, attains supreme perfection of inaction through renunciation.

[gita-a18-v50] As one who has attained perfection reaches brahman, so know from me in brief, O son of Kunti, the supreme steadfastness of knowledge.

[gita-a18-v51] Joined with purified intellect, restraining the self by firmness, abandoning sound and other objects, and casting away attachment and aversion.

[gita-a18-v52] Dwelling in seclusion, eating lightly, restraining speech, body, and mind, devoted to meditation yoga, always taking refuge in dispassion.

[gita-a18-v53] Having released ego, strength, pride, desire, anger, and possession, free from mine-ness and peaceful, one becomes fit for brahman-becoming.

[gita-a18-v54] Becoming brahman, with clear self, one neither grieves nor rejoices, is equal toward all beings, and obtains supreme devotion to me.

[gita-a18-v55] By devotion one truly knows me, and having truly known me, enters into me thereafter.

[gita-a18-v56] Doing all actions always while taking refuge in me, one obtains the eternal imperishable station by my grace.

[gita-a18-v57] Dedicating all actions to me by mind, O Bharata, taking refuge in discernment-yoga, be always of mind fixed on me.

[gita-a18-v58] With mind fixed on me you will cross all difficulties by my grace; but if you refuse from ego, you will not be freed and will perish.

[gita-a18-v59] Thinking 'relying on ego I will not fight' is false; your resolve is false, and nature will compel you.

[gita-a18-v60] Bound by innate nature to action, one must perform actions with my declared knowledge as authority; then bondage ceases.

[gita-a18-v61] The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings and whirls them, mounted on the machine of maya.

[gita-a18-v62] Go to that very refuge with whole being; by his grace you will obtain the eternal place.

[gita-a18-v63] Thus this knowledge, more secret than secret, has been declared by me; examine it completely and act as you wish.

[gita-a18-v64] Hear again my supreme word, most secret of all; because you are dear to me, I will speak what is beneficial.

[gita-a18-v65] Be of mind fixed on me, be my devotee, worship me, bow to me; you will come to me alone.

[gita-a18-v66] Abandoning all dharmas, go to me alone as refuge; I will liberate you from all sins, do not grieve.

[gita-a18-v67] This knowledge is not to be spoken to the unqualified; secrecy preserves its success, and envy toward the Lord is disrespect.

[gita-a18-v68] Whoever declares this supreme secret among devotees, making supreme devotion to the Lord, comes to the Lord without doubt.

[gita-a18-v69] No one among men will be a greater doer of what is dear to me, and no one else on earth is dearer.

[gita-a18-v70] Whoever studies this righteous dialogue of ours is worshipped by me through knowledge-sacrifice; this is my thought.

[gita-a18-v71] A faithful, non-envious man who hears this is also liberated and attains the auspicious worlds of meritorious acts.

[gita-a18-v72] Has this been heard by you, O son of Pṛthā, with one-pointed mind? Has ignorance-delusion been destroyed for you, O winner of wealth?

[gita-a18-v73] Arjuna says his delusion is gone, memory is gained by Krishna's grace, he stands free of doubt, and will do Krishna's word; the commentary notes that war-readiness has arisen, though full brahman-knowledge has not yet arisen.

[gita-a18-v74] Sanjaya says he heard this wondrous, hair-raising dialogue between Vasudeva's son and the great-souled Partha.

[gita-a18-v75] By Vyasa's grace he heard this more secret great yoga, spoken directly by Krishna, lord of yoga, himself.

[gita-a18-v76] O king, remembering again and again the wondrous, meritorious dialogue of Kesava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

[gita-a18-v77] And remembering again and again Hari's most wondrous form, wonder arises in me, O great king; I rejoice greatly again and again.

[gita-a18-v78] Where Krishna, lord of yoga, and Partha, bow-bearer, are, there are splendor, victory, certain prosperity, and policy; Sanjaya gathers the dialogue in firm order, and mere remembrance of it is said to give supreme Brahman, so that by mere remembrance of the Lord-Arjuna dialogue, through attainment of reality, splendor, victory, and powers arise.

[gita-a18-v79] Here is the summary verse: breaking the dark intellect, attaining Viṣṇu beyond discrimination, all becomes Śaṅkara; the eighteenth chapter of the Gītārthasaṃgraha composed by Abhinavagupta is complete, and Śiva is praised.
